title: W50NH9-27-R-A006 (formally W50NH9-26-R-A019) Scalable Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture Information Technology (IT) Contractor Manpower Equivalent (CME) Support (Scalable GEOINT)
description: RFP Number: W50NH9-27-R-A006 Requirement: Scalable Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture Information Technology (IT) Contractor Manpower Equivalent (CME) Support (Scalable GEOINT) for United States (U.S.) Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM) (also known as Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture Information Technology (IT)) 1. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) via SAM.gov. Interested Offerors are requested to submit a proposal in response to this RFP. You are to submit the proposal for your company no later than 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on Friday, 13 November 2026. A proposal validity period of no less than 240 calendar days from the proposal due date is required. 2. The Period of Performance (PoP) for one 30-day transition-in period (which is included in the base period), one 12-month base period, four 12-month option periods in accordance with (IAW) Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) FAR 52.217-9, and one six-month option period IAW RFO FAR 52.217-8. The estimated award date for this contract is 11 January 2027. The type of contract for this action will be primarily Time and Material. The Government will evaluate this requirement on a Best Value Trade Off basis, as detailed in Sections L and M of this RFP, proposals are not to include any Contract Line-Item Numbers (CLINs) other than those listed in the RFP. 3. All terms, conditions, and provisions set forth in this solicitation apply to this RFP and any resulting contract award. 4. The Offeror shall submit its proposal in accordance with the instructions included in Section L of this RFP. Any questions in regard to this RFP must be submitted no later than 11:59AM EST on Tuesday, 20 October 2026 via email to Contract Specialists Richard Schmidt (richard.a.schmidt4.civ@army.mil) and Cassandra Spadina (cassandra.e.spadina.civ@army.mil) and Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO) Brent Vergauwen (brent.k.vergauwen.civ@army.mil). The Government requests Offerors submit questions in a Microsoft (MS) Excel spreadsheet and identify the RFP or attachment page and paragraph related to the question. The Government reserves the right to not respond to questions received after this date and time. 5. Prospective Offerors are cautioned that this version of the RFP, inclusive of its attachments, is the final version of this solicitation. These files differ from those previously released in draft form. 6. If there are any discrepancies between questions and answers and the RFP (to include all amendments), the language of the RFP will govern. 7. Due to the transition from Fiscal Year 2026 to Fiscal Year 2027, the solicitation number for the Pre-solicitation Notice was updated from W50NH9-26-R-A019 to W50NH9-27-R-A006.

description: Sources Sought Notice This is a Sources Sought Notice (a) The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Sources Sought or to otherwise pay for the information solicited. (b) Although "proposal," "offeror," contractor, and "offeror" may be used in this sources sought notice, any response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. The Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. (c) Any information received from a contractor in response to this Sources Sought may be used in creating a solicitation. Any information received which is marked with a statement, such as "proprietary" or "confidential," intended to restrict distribution will not be distributed outside of the Government, except as required by law. (d) This Sources Sought is issued by VISN 2 Contracting Office in Buffalo, NY for the purpose of collecting information about the Syracuse VA Medical Center, located at 800 Irving Ave, Syracuse, NY 13210. The VA is seeking to provide for this requirement as of 3/1/2027 to establish a new service. The NAICS code identified for this requirement is 238210 with a size standard of $19 Million. The requirement is detailed in the Statement of Work attachment of this document. (e) Cursory market research has identified small businesses that may be able to provide for this requirement. Contractors that are able to meet the requirements in the attachment and possess an interest in performing these service, are encouraged to email a capability statement and full information to Leia LaBruna, Contract Specialist at Leia.Labruna@va.gov by November 13, 2026 by 12:00pm EST. - Part of the purpose of this sources sought is to determine the viability of set aside to a specific socio-economic category(service-disabled veteran owned small business, veteran owned small business, women owned small business, HUB Zone, 8(a), small business). Interested parties MUST provide company/individual name, a capability statement showing that your company has the ability to provide 100% of the requirement, examples of same or similar work performed at other facilities, SAM UEID number and address, point of contact and social-economic. title: Commercial Kennels/Boarding Military Working Dogs
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The Marine Corps Installations National Capital Region � Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), located at Marine Corps Base Quantico, VA, is conducting market research on behalf of the Provost Marshall Office Quantico VA. The purpose is to identify vendors capable of providing kennels and boarding for an estimated amount of 10 to 20 Military Working Dogs for an estimated time of 24 to 48 months. CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS: Marine Corps Installations � National Capital Region, Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR RCO), located on Marine Corps Base, 2010 Henderson Road, Quantico, VA. INTRODUCTION: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for market research and planning purposes. It provides industry an opportunity to ask questions and offer suggestions regarding the draft technical specifications outlined in the Capabilities Statement below. DISCLAIMER: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMAITON IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ). IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION: Estimated quantity: 10 to 20 Military working dogs Time: 24 to 48 months Requested starting date: 1 December 2025 or sooner or as soon as possible The minimum run size of 8x8 Facilities are required to be within the immediate geographic area of Quantico, Virginia. 24/7 access by us, and no access by anyone else to include kennel employees Break yard access dedicated to our MWDS Can not be housed or share common areas with other pets At least one Quarantine kennel (could be an option, as it would only be needed if a new dog arrives, or a dog gets ill) The following are only needed if we are completely barred from utilizing the current facility for non-housing (i.e., we can still use the works spaces and utilities and even bath the dogs, just can�t put them in the runs�) Storage for food and Medication Bathing station for MWD�s Feed Prep area with sink to clean food bowls and water bowls Washer and Dryer to clean equipment (towels, rags, sleeves) INDUSTRY FEEDBACK: This is a REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY to obtain industry�s feedback on the anticipated technical specifications, potential cost and performance risks, as well as any other related considerations for the required supplies/services. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely to gather industry feedback regarding the anticipated technical specifications, cost and performance risks, and other relevant considerations associated with the required supplies and/or services. Please provide input on the following: Capability: Can your organization deliver all products and services outlined in the Requirement Description? Barriers to Competition: Are there any conditions, certifications, or proprietary constraints that could limit fair competition? Proposal Interest: Are you likely to submit a proposal for this requirement? Please explain your reasoning. Commercial Availability: Is this product/service commonly available in the commercial market? Pricing Structure: Can this requirement be fulfilled under a Firm Fixed Price contract? Competition Influencers: Are there any specific conditions, requirements, or limitations that could affect open and fair competition? Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing gives the draft requirements. If unable to generate estimates at this stage, specify what additional information would be needed. Pricing should reflect all costs associated with course development and delivery, including travel expenses, if applicable. Please note that the ROM pricing is non-binding and shall not be construed as a formal pricing proposal. NAICS Classification: What North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code(s) best align with this requirement? SUBMISSION DETAILS: Submissions shall reference RFI No. �M00264-26-RFI-001A �Boarding for Military Working Dogs� in the subject line. Interested vendors who wish to respond to this RFI should send responses no later than 12:00PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 13 November 2025, via email to the following email addresses: hal.d.jones@usmc.mil and sharon.palustre@usmc.mil. Request responses shall be provided in no more than 4 pages. Questions and comments regarding this requirement will be accepted, reviewed and answered if the Government determines responses are warranted. The Government will not consider any vendor email that is incomplete or is not addressing this RFI questions. The Government reserves the right to determine if a response addresses this RFI, is not complete, and/or to not review a response without any further communication with the vendor supplying the information. Submissions must include: 1) Responses to the �Industry Feedback� section of this RFI. 2) Business name and address. 3) Name of company representative, their business title and insurance. 4) Type of Business. 5) Cage Code and UEI; and 6) Contract vehicles that would be available to the Government for the procurement of the service, to include General Service Administration (GSA), Federal Supply Schedules (FSS), or any other Government Agency contract vehicle. (This information is for market research only and does not preclude your company from responding to this notice.) 8) Delivery Information Estimate lead time. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION: Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all materials. All information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. All government personnel reviewing RFI responses understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information as described in 41 USC 423. The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified.

description: **************************************************************************************************************************************************** NOTICE OF EXTENSION OF QUOTATION RECEIPT DATE (SOLICITATION N0017826R2500) In accordance with FAR 12.603(c)(4), notice is hereby given that the quotation submission deadline for Solicitation N0017826R2500 (DNA Warehousing Support) is EXTENDED from Thursday, 29 October 2026, to Friday, 13 November 2026, at 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). title: Request for Information (RFI): Verification and Compliance Checking for Natural-Language Network Requirements (FastVacc)
description: Modern networks need to be reconfigured quickly in response to mission changes or emerging threats, but checking compliance with security requirements can take months. This creates a window in which adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities introduced by those changes. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Information Processing Techniques Office (IPTO) seeks information on approaches, tools and practices for closing that window by reducing, by 2-3 orders of magnitude, the time and cost of verifiable compliance checking. DARPA envisions a capability that would take as input two items: (a) a requirements document written in natural language and (b) the configurations in a concrete network. In an offline phase, it would reason about the requirements for inconsistency, redundancy and incompleteness, and output consistent, non-redundant and completed requirements. Then, it would check, in near real-time, whether the concrete configurations satisfy all of the requirements. In all cases, its output would be understandable by a human.

description: THERE HAS BEEN ONE AMENDMENT TO THIS SOLICITATION SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS PART 1 � GENERAL INFORMATION 1. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

description: SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS NOTE: The Addendum cites solicitation W51AA1-26-Q-A100 instead of W51AA1-27-Q-A010 twice. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

Introduction and Background Objectives The National Center for Translational Sciences (NCATS) requires a partner to facilitate user administration, process/workflow improvements, content development/moderation, requirements gathering, and dissemination of the SMART IRB (Streamlined, Multisite, Accelerated Resources for Trials Institutional Review Board) portfolio of services. SMART IRB relies on three systems: (1) the SMARTIRB.org website which is used for content distribution, notification, and educational purposes, (2) Joinder, through which institutions enter institutional information and sign the SMART IRB Authorization Agreement (AA), and (3) the Online Reliance System (ORS), through which Institutional Review Board (IRB) reliance arrangements under the SMART IRB Agreement are documented on a study-by-study basis. description: The goal of this acquisition is to acquire a contractor that offers a full range of (1) clinical research services, including clinical research management, statistical design and analysis, protocol development and data management, clinical site management, pharmacovigilance services, quality assurance, and regulatory affairs support; (2) specialty services, including DSMB services; (3) analytical solutions, including bioinformatics, and (4) integrated clinical trial management through an organized system of tracking clinical trials. The contractor should be capable of providing these services, as required under the individual task orders, to support NHGRI clinical research protocols and related activities within the scope of this IDIQ contract. The main features of work includes: Provide and install one (1) new medium voltage switch gear. Provide and install one (1) new low voltage switch gear. title: Tobyhanna Gates & Turnstiles
description: SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS PART 1 � GENERAL INFORMATION 1. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: 27 October 2026: P00002 Updated PWS dated 27 October 2026. Post Round 1-3 Q&A's. 23 October 2026: P00001 Extend the due date to 13 November 2026. **Please take note that the solicitation number has been updated to HTC71127QE127 due to overlap in Fiscal Years** The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

The purpose of this procurement is to acquire autonomous healthcare delivery robot system for interior use at the VA Long Beach Healthcare System Pharmacy (VALBHS). 1. Functional and Performance Requirements The system shall autonomously transport and deliver critical Pharmacy medical supplies, pharmacy orders, and similar healthcare items within interior areas of VA Long Beach without continuous human teleoperation during normal operation. The system shall employ self driving obstacle avoidance technology that uses at least two sensing modalities from among 3D vision, eye safe laser ranging, and sonar (or functionally equivalent technologies) to map and navigate the facility while avoiding people and obstacles in a dynamic hospital environment. The robot shall be capable of continuous transport operations at a nominal walking pace appropriate for safe operation among staff and patients (approximately 2 4 miles per hour), with the ability to adjust speed as needed to comply with VA safety policies. 2. Payload and Capacity The robot shall provide at least one lockable, top loading cargo compartment designed for interior healthcare use. The primary cargo compartment shall have a total internal volume of at least 41 liters (approximately 11 gallons). The cargo compartment shall support a minimum payload of 50 pounds of medical items (e.g., linens, infusion pumps, towels, pharmacy totes, blood products, specimen racks). The system shall include configurable or removable internal accessories (e.g., liners, trays, baskets, or equivalent) that allow safe carriage of a variety of healthcare items such as prescription medications, 24 hour urine bottles, IV bags, test tube racks, and food containers commonly used at VA Long Beach. 3. Physical Characteristics The mobile robot width shall not exceed approximately 20 inches, enabling safe passage through standard VA corridors, doorways, and elevators. The overall height of the robot shall be approximately 37 inches to maintain visibility and accessibility for staff in nurse stations and corridors. The system shall be constructed of sturdy, resilient, easy to clean materials suitable for VA clinical environments, with smooth exterior surfaces compatible with commonly used hospital grade disinfectants. 4. Power and Endurance The robot shall support at least 24 hours of operation in a typical healthcare duty cycle with intermittent charging (i.e., the robot automatically or manually docks to recharge between runs without being removed from service for a full working day). The system shall include a docking/charging station compatible with standard 110 volt AC power, with a footprint not exceeding approximately 18 inches wide by 8 inches high by 10 inches deep. 5. Navigation and Maneuverability The robot shall support multiple navigation modes, including point to point delivery and other facility defined behaviors (e.g., delivery, usher, mingle, or functionally equivalent modes) that support VA logistics and clinical workflows. The robot shall have an effective turning radius of 0 feet (i.e., shall be capable of point turns in place) to maneuver in tight spaces such as corridors, patient room entries, and pharmacy/laboratory areas. 6. Communications and User Interface The system shall communicate with facility infrastructure using secure wireless communication, including Wi Fi; support for wide area connectivity (e.g., LTE or equivalent) is desired or shall be offered if commercially available. The system shall allow VA staff to initiate, monitor, and manage deliveries through a user interface appropriate for clinical and logistics personnel with minimal training (e.g., on robot touchscreen, workstation client, or mobile application). The user interface shall provide clear, task oriented controls and shall avoid vague performance descriptors such as user friendly or fastest, consistent with sound salient characteristics practices. 7. Environment and Support The system shall be designed and configured for interior use in VA healthcare facilities, including inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, ancillary services, and associated clinical spaces. The contractor shall provide technical and maintenance support appropriate for 24/7/365 VA healthcare operations (e.g., remote support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement or repair procedures), consistent with commercial practices for mission critical hospital equipment. 8. Trade Agreements Act and Domestic Preference The offered robot system (including docking station and integrated software) shall comply with applicable Trade Agreements Act (TAA) requirements and other domestic preference requirements referenced in the RFQ, as implemented in FAR Part 25 and applicable VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) clauses, as incorporated by the Contracting Officer. Offerors shall identify the country(ies) of origin of the end product(s) and shall certify compliance with TAA and applicable Buy American/domestic preference requirements in accordance with the solicitation s FAR/VAAR provisions and clauses. If an offered end product is not TAA compliant or domestic, the offeror shall clearly disclose this in its quotation so that the VA Contracting Officer can determine acceptability and apply any required price evaluation preferences or restrictions. 9. Competitive, Non Brand Name Basis These salient characteristics are expressed as minimums or approximate maximums (e.g., at least, not to exceed approximately ) to allow full and open competition; no specific brand name or model is required. Any commercial item that meets or exceeds all enumerated salient characteristics shall be considered technically acceptable, subject to the RFQ s evaluation criteria (e.g., price and past performance) and all other terms and conditions. Descriptive literature submitted with quotations shall clearly demonstrate how the quoted product meets or exceeds each salient characteristic; literature that merely reproduces marketing claims without quantifying key performance metrics may be deemed insufficient. title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: 23 October 2026: P00001 Extend the due date to 13 November 2026. **Please take note that the solicitation number has been updated to HTC71127QE127 due to overlap in Fiscal Years** The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

title: Nutrition Care Services; Military Treatment Facilities - Forts Irwin, Leonard Wood, Riley, Stewart, and West Point
description: RFP HT940827RE003 is amended on 5 November 2026 to make the following changes: 1. Provide a "fillable" SF 1449 for Offerors to complete unit (i.e, by month) pricing and extended (i.e., number of months multiplied by monthly price) pricing. This SF 1449 is uploaded below; Offerors shall use either the 5 Nov 2026 or 30 Oct 2026 version when submitting their proposal. All other instructions for completing the SF 1449 still apply. NOTE: No SF 30s have been issued for this solicitation. 2. Provide additional Government Answers to Vendor Questions that were not answered previously. There will not be an update to Technical Exhibit E at this time; the awardee(s) will be able to tour each MTF during the transition period. 3. The due date and time for receipt of proposals remains Friday, 13 November 2026 at 1200pm (noon) Central via email to the POCs listed below. Offerors are reminded that it is their responsibility to ensure all documents are received by the POCs by the established closing date and time. ///////////////// RFP HT940827RE003 is amended on 30 October 2026 to make the following changes: 1. Extend closing due date and time for receipt of proposals to Friday, 13 November 2026 at 1200pm (noon) Central. 2. Update various Attachments and Exhibits. See list below - any attachments/exhibits with a date of "30 Oct 2026" are NEW versions (i.e., updated) as of this amendment. Changes are in red font where applicable. The previous versions are hereby deleted. The previous version of Attachment 4 (Past Performance Questionnare) may still be used, but must follow the updated submission instructions (eg, directly to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist). Any attachment/exhibit without a date remain as originally uploaded (ie, no changes). 3. Provide Government Answers to Vendor Questions. The Government anticipates providing further answers NLT Wednesday, 4 November 2026 and an updated Technical Exhibit E, but does not anticipate these will materially impact a proposal; therefore, no further extensions to the due date for receipt of proposals are anticipated. No further questions will be accepted. ///////////////// Nutrition Care Food Service, Various Military Medical Treatment Facilities The solicitation number for the below-described requirement is HT940827RE003. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 722310, Food Service Contractors, which has a size standard of $47 million. This requirement was previously announced, but never solicited, under ID: HT940826RE017. The Government has updated some of the documents that were previously posted as a result of questions asked since the initial posting; if an interested party still has questions or feels that any information is still unclear, they are encouraged to submit those questions to the POCs listed herein. The Defense Health Agency has a requirement for non-personal services providing qualified labor and management necessary to perform nutrition care food management, supervisory, technical, administrative, and clerical services that focus primarily on the following areas: dining facility management functions, therapeutic food preparation, patient tray assembly and delivery service, clinical training, facility sanitation, janitorial duties as it relates to the services being provided, and the associated logistics analysis and management functions in support of the Nutrition Care Divisions for five (5) Military Medical Treatment Facilities (MTFs). The following MTFs requiring the Nutrition Care Food Service support are: Weed Army Community Hospital (Fort Irwin, California), General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri), Irwin Army Community Hospital (Fort Riley, Kansas), Winn Army Community Hospital (Fort Stewart, Georgia), and Keller Army Community Hospital (West Point, New York). A transition period of 1 December 2026 � 31 January 2027, base period of 1 February 2027 � 30 September 2027, and two (2) twelve-month option periods through 30 September 2029 are contemplated. The contract will be firm-fixed-price, with a set monthly price established per MTF. Multiple contracts may be awarded, up to one (1) per MTF. The Randolph Sheppard Act (RSA) applies to this requirement; therefore, priority will be given to any responsive State Licensing Agency (SLA) pursuant to the RSA. The priority established by the RSA applies to the award of contracts for the operation of cafeterias on Federal property. NOTE: The evaluation criteria will be the same for all offerors, including any responsible SLA. However, the solicitation will be issued on a full-and-open basis with a small business participation (eg, subcontracting) plan as one of the evaluation criteria for other-than-small businesses and non-SLAs. The solicitation will be issued on or about 16 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 4 November 2026. Questions are due via email to the POCs listed below by 22 October 2026. The solicitation and all associated documents necessary for preparing a proposal are posted on sam.gov. Interested vendors are encouraged to contact the POCs listed below with any questions they may have, including about the attachments. This notice does not in itself represent the issuance of a formal request for proposals and is not intended to be taken as such. Prospective offerors are advised that if tentatively selected for award, they must register with the System for Award Management (SAM) (http://www.sam.gov) and obtain a Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) prior to any award being made. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be physically issued, and telephone and faxed requests for the solicitation will not be honored. Interested parties are urged to visit SAM frequently for any updates/amendments to any and all documents. All questions regarding this notice are to be submitted in writing via e-mail to the listed POCs. Please use the solicitation number �HT940827RE003� in the subject line of all correspondence. All questions submitted are subject to be posted in this notice and the associated solicitation, along with the appropriate response(s). Vendor identities will not be disclosed. Prospective Offerors must comply with all the requirements of the solicitation and any attachments thereto to be considered responsive.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: 04 November 2026: P0003 Revised SOR. 27 October 2026: P0002 Updated PWS dated 27 October 2026. Post Round 1-3 Q&A's. 23 October 2026: P0001 Extend the due date to 13 November 2026. **Please take note that the solicitation number has been updated to HTC71127QE127 due to overlap in Fiscal Years** The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

title: Cost Per Reportable Result Purchase of Immunohistochemistry Reagents for Laboratory Tests.
description: The VA Puget Sound Health Care System Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service requires a histology staining workflow system which includes: Two (2) immunohistochemistry (IHC) and two (2) in-situ hybridization (ISH) immunostainers, and two (2) special stainers, and a specimen tracking system which promotes proper identification of specimens and slides and will audit workflow to identify areas that need improvement and reduce errors. The tracking system will improve patient safety, provide a chain of custody, and will monitor productivity. All the components of the workflow system must communicate with each other in order to track the workflow. The stainers attached to this system must be automated and allow the system to track and label slides for special staining and immunostaining. The workflow system must be compatible with the IT systems VISTA and/or Cerner, as well as any other new electronic health record system the VA acquires and also be compatible with Data Innovations middleware.

title: 6515--Autonomous Healthcare Delivery Robot
description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION ABOUT PRICING, DELIVERY, THE MARKET, AND CAPABILITIES IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI FOR PLANNING PURPOSES IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT/RFI DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice / RFI only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice / RFI is to gain information about potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI, further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcements may be published. The purpose of this procurement is to acquire autonomous healthcare delivery robot system for interior use at the VA Long Beach Healthcare System Pharmacy (VALBHS). 1. Functional and Performance Requirements The system shall autonomously transport and deliver critical Pharmacy medical supplies, pharmacy orders, and similar healthcare items within interior areas of VA Long Beach without continuous human teleoperation during normal operation. The system shall employ self driving obstacle avoidance technology that uses at least two sensing modalities from among 3D vision, eye safe laser ranging, and sonar (or functionally equivalent technologies) to map and navigate the facility while avoiding people and obstacles in a dynamic hospital environment. The robot shall be capable of continuous transport operations at a nominal walking pace appropriate for safe operation among staff and patients (approximately 2 4 miles per hour), with the ability to adjust speed as needed to comply with VA safety policies. 2. Payload and Capacity The robot shall provide at least one lockable, top loading cargo compartment designed for interior healthcare use. The primary cargo compartment shall have a total internal volume of at least 41 liters (approximately 11 gallons). The cargo compartment shall support a minimum payload of 50 pounds of medical items (e.g., linens, infusion pumps, towels, pharmacy totes, blood products, specimen racks). The system shall include configurable or removable internal accessories (e.g., liners, trays, baskets, or equivalent) that allow safe carriage of a variety of healthcare items such as prescription medications, 24 hour urine bottles, IV bags, test tube racks, and food containers commonly used at VA Long Beach. 3. Physical Characteristics The mobile robot width shall not exceed approximately 20 inches, enabling safe passage through standard VA corridors, doorways, and elevators. The overall height of the robot shall be approximately 37 inches to maintain visibility and accessibility for staff in nurse stations and corridors. The system shall be constructed of sturdy, resilient, easy to clean materials suitable for VA clinical environments, with smooth exterior surfaces compatible with commonly used hospital grade disinfectants. 4. Power and Endurance The robot shall support at least 24 hours of operation in a typical healthcare duty cycle with intermittent charging (i.e., the robot automatically or manually docks to recharge between runs without being removed from service for a full working day). The system shall include a docking/charging station compatible with standard 110 volt AC power, with a footprint not exceeding approximately 18 inches wide by 8 inches high by 10 inches deep. 5. Navigation and Maneuverability The robot shall support multiple navigation modes, including point to point delivery and other facility defined behaviors (e.g., delivery, usher, mingle, or functionally equivalent modes) that support VA logistics and clinical workflows. The robot shall have an effective turning radius of 0 feet (i.e., shall be capable of point turns in place) to maneuver in tight spaces such as corridors, patient room entries, and pharmacy/laboratory areas. 6. Communications and User Interface The system shall communicate with facility infrastructure using secure wireless communication, including Wi Fi; support for wide area connectivity (e.g., LTE or equivalent) is desired or shall be offered if commercially available. The system shall allow VA staff to initiate, monitor, and manage deliveries through a user interface appropriate for clinical and logistics personnel with minimal training (e.g., on robot touchscreen, workstation client, or mobile application). The user interface shall provide clear, task oriented controls and shall avoid vague performance descriptors such as user friendly or fastest, consistent with sound salient characteristics practices. 7. Environment and Support The system shall be designed and configured for interior use in VA healthcare facilities, including inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, ancillary services, and associated clinical spaces. The contractor shall provide technical and maintenance support appropriate for 24/7/365 VA healthcare operations (e.g., remote support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement or repair procedures), consistent with commercial practices for mission critical hospital equipment. 8. Trade Agreements Act and Domestic Preference The offered robot system (including docking station and integrated software) shall comply with applicable Trade Agreements Act (TAA) requirements and other domestic preference requirements referenced in the RFQ, as implemented in FAR Part 25 and applicable VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) clauses, as incorporated by the Contracting Officer. Offerors shall identify the country(ies) of origin of the end product(s) and shall certify compliance with TAA and applicable Buy American/domestic preference requirements in accordance with the solicitation s FAR/VAAR provisions and clauses. If an offered end product is not TAA compliant or domestic, the offeror shall clearly disclose this in its quotation so that the VA Contracting Officer can determine acceptability and apply any required price evaluation preferences or restrictions. 9. Competitive, Non Brand Name Basis These salient characteristics are expressed as minimums or approximate maximums (e.g., at least, not to exceed approximately ) to allow full and open competition; no specific brand name or model is required. Any commercial item that meets or exceeds all enumerated salient characteristics shall be considered technically acceptable, subject to the RFQ s evaluation criteria (e.g., price and past performance) and all other terms and conditions. Descriptive literature submitted with quotations shall clearly demonstrate how the quoted product meets or exceeds each salient characteristic; literature that merely reproduces marketing claims without quantifying key performance metrics may be deemed insufficient. title: W912BU27QA002: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - 911 Emergency Dispatch Services
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Philadelphia District, intends to solicit and award a sole-source contract to the County of Berks, Pennsylvania, for 911 emergency dispatch services. The requirement includes emergency communications and dispatch coordination services necessary to support Government operations within the designated service area. Berks County Department of Emergency Services operates the sole public safety answering point and countywide radio dispatch infrastructure within Berks County, PA. They maintain exclusive, direct communications and dispatch oversight for all local municipal police, fire departments, ambulance and rescue squads, and emergency services operating in the jurisdiction encompassing Blue Marsh Lake. Consequently, no other private or commercial entity possesses the jurisdictional authority, public safety communication network, or direct interoperability necessary to dispatch emergency services and cross-communicate with USACE Natural Resource and Park Ranger staff in this operational area. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO FAR 13.106-1(b)(1) based on the determination that the identified source is the only reasonably available source capable of meeting the Governments requirements. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can satisfy the requirement may submit a capability statement for Government consideration. All responses received by the stated deadline will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether conducting a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government reserves the right to proceed with the intended sole-source acquisition, consistent with applicable acquisition regulations. All responses must be submitted via email to Cierra.R.Vega@usace.army.mil AND Jessica.A.Hazen@usace.army.mil no later than 13 November 2026, at 1:00 PM Eastern Standard Time.

title: Quality Assurance Services - Civil Works, Interagency and International Services (IIS), and Military Construction Projects in Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District issues this Request for Proposals (RFP) to award an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Quality Assurance Services across Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. This procurement follows the presolicitation notice previously synopsized under solicitation number W51DQV26RA007. The contractor shall provide comprehensive quality assurance oversight supporting Civil Works, International and Interagency Services (IIS), and Military Construction (MILCON) projects, including navigation, flood risk management, coastal protection, environmental restoration, water resources, and military or federal installations. Services encompass monitoring contractor compliance with plans and specifications, reviewing engineering submittals and technical reports, conducting on-site field inspections of dams, levees, berms, cutoff walls, pump stations, flood control gates, and electrical systems, and performing certified sampling and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, and water. Contract personnel shall also perform daily safety monitoring and prepare daily quality assurance inspection reports. This action is a total small business set-aside under NAICS code 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) with an applicable small business size standard of $19.5 million. The contract ordering period comprises a one-year base period, four 12-month option periods, and one six-month option period, not to exceed a total duration of five years and six months, with a maximum program capacity of $35 million across the contract life.

title: E-Waste Collection Events
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance LLC (BEA), the Management and Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified recyclers capable of organizing residential electronic waste (e-waste) collection events in states without e-waste recycling regulation (i.e., nonregulated states) to support INL�s research and operational mission. This service is essential for raising awareness, increasing collection volumes and verifying whether successful collection methods from a regulated state can be applied to a nonregulated state with comparable results. Eligible states for this work include Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Idaho (except eastern and southeastern region), Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, Tennessee and Wyoming. BACKGROUND BEA is the Management and Operating Contractor for the DOE located at INL. INL is a DOE national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security and advanced energy innovation. A BEA research team has the lead role on the DOE project titled, �Comparing Strategies to Collect Battery-Containing Devices in States with and without Electronics Recycling Laws.� The proposed service will operate to support this project through Sept. 30, 2027. In the first two years of this project, project teams organized collection events in New York and Idaho. New York is as urban area with established e-waste regulations, and Idaho is a rural area without such requirements. By applying successful collection methods from New York to southeastern Idaho, we observed similar success across 20 e-waste collection events. To further validate these results, we are seeking opportunities to apply our methods in other nonregulated states by organizing six to nine e-waste collection events. SCOPE OF WORK Responding organizations must be capable of delivering the following services: Provide existing status; compile data from existing residential collection activities related to seasonal trends, locations and e-waste types. Organize collection events at new locations in nonregulated states, with each participating organization conducting at least two to three collection events before September 2027. Arrange advertisements on multiple channels to broadcast new collection events and raise awareness about battery-containing e-waste recycling. Provide collection event data including number of participants and quantities of collected e-waste by type PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an EOI that includes the following: Organization information: Organization name, address, organization type, scope of operations, number of employees and primary point of contact. Existing e-waste collection access: Describe existing e-waste collection events, permanent drop-off locations or other collection options available in the proposed service area. Program interest and expected outcomes: Explain why your organization wants to participate in this project and what outcomes you expect to achieve. Service area and target participants: Identify the cities, counties, or communities that will be served by the proposed e-waste collection activities. Community need: Describe the primary e-waste management challenges or unmet needs in the proposed service area. Collection plan: Describe the proposed e-waste collection activities for the program year (by Sept. 1, 2027). Provide the anticipated number of collection events and proposed cities, counties, or collection locations. Provide communication strategies (i.e. social media, mail, news, flyers, etc.) to raise awareness and promote collection events. Downstream e-waste management: Identify who will transport, receive, recycle, process, or otherwise manage the collected e-waste. Recycler/processor qualifications: Identify relevant certifications or qualifications of the entities handling collected e-waste, such as R2, e-Stewards, or other applicable certifications. Partnership with local nonprofit organizations or local authorities: Specify whether the proposed e-waste collection activities involve collaboration with local nonprofit organizations or governmental authorities. Deadline for submission: Nov. 13, 2026 (date subject to change) Submit to: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov Technical Point of Contact: ThiThuyTien.Le@inl.gov Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated Request for Proposal solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

title: Sources Sought for the Recapitalization of the Navy�s High Voltage (230kV) Transmission Loop and all Ancillary Equipment at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, GA
description: THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR EITHER A QUOTE OR PROPOSAL OR AN INVITATION FOR A BID. THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO RECAPITALIZE THE NAVY HIGH VOLTAGE 230KV TRANSMISSION LOOP AND ALL ANCILLARY EQUIPMENT AND GEAR AT NAVAL SUBMARINE BASE KINGS BAY, GEORGIA. THE WORK MUST COMPLY WITH ALL APPLICABLE NAVAL AND UTILITY PROVIDER PHYSICAL AND CYBERSECURITY REQUIREMENTS. IT REQUIRES SEAMLESS COORDINATION AND A SINGLE POINT OF ACCOUNTABILITY FOR EXECUTION WITHOUT UNNECESSARY SERVICE DISRUPTIONS OR DELAYS. NO SOLICITATION OR SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE CURRENTLY AVAILABLE. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of qualified and interested participants in any of the following categories. These include large business, small business, 8(a) business development participants, HUBZone small business concerns, service-disabled veteran-owned small business concerns, veteran-owned small business concerns, and women-owned small business concerns. Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, security-cleared personnel, security approvals, equipment, financial capability, and cybersecurity certifications relative to the project. The project entails utility infrastructure upgrades and connection facilities for the Navy-owned and operated 230kV electrical power transmission loop that services NSB Kings Bay, Georgia. The recapitalized infrastructure must be capable of safely and reliably interconnecting with the regional 230kV transmission grid. Prior experience in coordinating high-voltage interconnections with a regulated utility provider is an essential requirement. Capabilities including live-line interconnection work, secure supply chain management, and cybersecurity expertise (e.g., NERC CIP, DoD UFC 4-010-06 for Industrial Control Systems) are considered essential for the timely and cost-effective completion of the project without coordination delays or interoperability concerns. The Government contemplates an acquisition to accomplish the wholesale recapitalization and cybersecurity hardening of the Navy-owned high-voltage transmission line and associated gear at NSB Kings Bay, Georgia. The modernized on-base grid will remain solely under the operational control of the U.S. Navy and is intended to service only the installation. The system must be designed to safely coordinate with the regional transmission utility for grid stability and reliability at the point of interconnection. Work will include relocation of the high power loop and crossing tower across the North River to a geotechnically stable site. It includes replacement of conductors along the primary transmission corridor. The new installation must meet all required Department of Defense and industry cybersecurity standards. This includes the wholesale modernization of substation digital protective relays with utility-grade devices and the implementation of a secure, encrypted Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. The Government�s SCADA system must be capable of providing necessary operational coordination and data exchange with the utility provider�s dispatch center via a secure communications gateway. The contractor will replace closed circuit television metering transformers with fault monitoring capability. The work requires replacement of porcelain insulators, high-voltage bushings, surge arrestors, and ground-grid bonding systems ensuring compatibility with incoming power feed loads and feeds. The contractor must remove manual or gang-operated air disconnect switches at the entry bays of Substations 1 through 3. The project includes installation of smart supervisory-controlled Motor-Operated Disconnects and vacuum or SF6 circuit breakers equipped with high-speed differential bus and transformer protection schemes. It also requires wholesale modernization of substation digital protective relays utility-grade devices with full coordination between the encrypted installation Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) telemetry. All telemetry and relay configurations must comply with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (EIP) standards. They must also comply with applicable DoD Unified Facilities Criteria 4-010-06 for Industrial Control Systems (ICS) standards and ad-hoc compatibility with existing utility infrastructure as determined by the agency. The anticipated period of performance is approximately 900 calendar days from award. The estimated magnitude for this procurement is between $100,000,000 to $250,000,000. The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) is 221122 for Electric Power Distribution with a small business size standard of 1,100 employees. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and the Government will not accept them to form a binding contract. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. The Government will use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement of the subject requirement. Industry will be notified of the results of the market research via the pre-solicitation or synopsis notice as applicable. GPC owns and operates the regional 230kV transmission grid that provides bulk power to the NSB Kings Bay point of interconnection. Any contractor performing this work must deliver a system that meets all relevant industry standards for protection, control, and communications (e.g., NERC, IEEE) to ensure safe and reliable grid operations. The design must allow for the necessary exchange of telemetry and operational data with GPC to ensure grid stability, without requiring the use of any proprietary utility software, hardware, or protocols on the government-owned portion of the system. Interested and responsible parties experienced in wholesale high-voltage power line work in Tier 3 security military installations with all necessary credentials and accreditations for both applicable naval and regional integration and interoperability standards should identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement. We place special emphasis on cybersecurity specifications and supply chain security. Interested and responsible parties should use the attached questionnaire to respond to this notice. Responses to this notice must be submitted in electronic Adobe PDF format and attached to an email addressed to ryan.d.bell16.civ@us.navy.mil and rebecca.m.jones75.civ@us.navy.mil. Please identify �Recapitalize 230kV Transmission Loop at NSB Kings Bay� in the subject line of your response. Responses are limited to 5 pages in length and 5MB in size. You should only include the information requested in the attached questionnaire. Do not submit brochures or other corporate marketing information. The due date for responses is 1400 hours EDT on 13 November 2026. Responses received by the due date and time of this notice will be considered by the Government. Any questions submitted via email to the recipients identified above prior to the due date for responses will be considered. No additional questions will be addressed. Interested parties are responsible for verifying receipt of communications. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. IN ORDER TO PROTECT THE PROCUREMENT INTEGRITY OF ANY FUTURE PROCUREMENT ARISING FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT, INFORMATION REGARDING THE TECHNICAL POINT OF CONTACT WILL NOT BE GIVEN AND NO APPOINTMENTS FOR PRESENTATIONS WILL BE MADE.

description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. Phase I proposals must be submitted electronically through the Department of Defense Secure Access File Exchange (DoD SAFE). The question submission period remains unchanged at 1400 Easter Time on October 14, 2025. This amendment does not extend the proposal due date. Except as expressly modified by Amendment A00001, all other terms and conditions remain unchanged. -------------------------------- Amendment A00002 -------------------------------- The United States Coast Guard (USCG) hereby issues Amendment A00002 to Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001, originally issued on SAM.gov on September 30, 2026. Amendment A00002 incorporates an updated Attachment 1, Questions and Answers, which shall be used by prospective Offerors to submit any future questions and requests for clarification in accordance with Section L.4 of the solicitation. The question submission period remains unchanged at 1400 Easter Time on October 14, 2025. This amendment does not extend the proposal due date. Phase I proposals remain due no later than 1400 Eastern Time on November 13, 2026. Offerors shall review Amendment A00002 and all associated attachments in their entirety and shall acknowledge receipt of this amendment in accordance with the solicitation instructions. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. title: P-25A Hand Pump Kits
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division Lakehurst, NJ intends to solicit and negotiate on a sole source basis with The Entwistle Company (CAGE 20722) located in Hudson, MA for the procurement of Quantity one (1) prototype kit, and seventy-two (72) production Hand Pump Kits in support of the P-25A Shipboard Firefighting Vehicle Program. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.
