title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. Proposal Submission Phase I proposals are due: 13 November 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time All proposal submissions shall be made in accordance with Section L of the solicitation. Phase I proposals must be submitted electronically through the Department of Defense Secure Access File Exchange (DoD SAFE). In accordance with Section L.3(b), Offerors shall email the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than five (5) working days prior to the proposal due date to request a DoD SAFE Drop-Off Request. Questions and Requests for Clarification Questions shall be submitted in accordance with Section L no later than: 14 October 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time Questions received after this date may not be answered. Government responses may be issued through solicitation questions and answers and/or formal solicitation amendment, as appropriate. Solicitation Documents and Restricted GFI See the Attachments/Links section below for the solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents associated with this RFP. Certain Government Furnished Information identified in Section J is authorized under Distribution Statement C and will not be publicly posted to SAM.gov. Authorized Offerors requiring access to these documents shall submit a written request by email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist. Following verification of the requester�s authorization to receive the material, the Government will transmit the applicable documents through DoD SAFE. -------------------------------- Amendment A00001 -------------------------------- The United States Coast Guard (USCG) hereby issues Amendment A00001 to Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001, originally issued on SAM.gov on September 30, 2026. Amendment A00001 is issued to provide the Government�s responses to questions received, incorporate a standardized document for future vendor question submissions, and provide advance notice regarding anticipated future solicitation revisions. Amendment A00001 incorporates Attachment 2, Questions and Government Responses v1, containing Government responses to Questions 1 through 53. Questions 1 through 46 provide responses to vendor inquiries submitted during the presolicitation phase under Presolicitation Notice USCG-RB-S-III-2026. title: Vacuum Turbo Pumps
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing Turbomolecular Pumping Stations. The Turbomolecular Pumping Station (TMPS) will replace the Agilent Technologies/Varian TPS-compact TV301 (Model: 969-8221M003), which contains the following components: TV301 turbomolecular pump, integrated controller, variable leak valve and dry scroll backing pump. The manufacturer (Agilent/Varian) has discontinued this item and ceased its support of the key components. This acquisition will aid AFMETCAL in maintaining support for a multitude of different high-vacuum and vacuum metrology calibration equipment across the Air Force. The new standard would support high-vacuum chambers, vacuum sensors, transducers, and other similar high-vacuum TMDE. The TMPS shall evacuate vacuum TMDE up to high-vacuum levels in absolute mode. Responses will assist AFMETCAL in determining the availability of qualified sources and the appropriate acquisition strategy. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity of 86 units over 5 years. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 27M-083A-VA in all correspondence. title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. Proposal Submission Phase I proposals are due: 13 November 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time All proposal submissions shall be made in accordance with Section L of the solicitation. Phase I proposals must be submitted electronically through the Department of Defense Secure Access File Exchange (DoD SAFE). In accordance with Section L.3(b), Offerors shall email the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than five (5) working days prior to the proposal due date to request a DoD SAFE Drop-Off Request. Questions and Requests for Clarification Questions shall be submitted in accordance with Section L no later than: 14 October 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time Questions received after this date may not be answered. Government responses may be issued through solicitation questions and answers and/or formal solicitation amendment, as appropriate. Solicitation Documents and Restricted GFI See the Attachments/Links section below for the solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents associated with this RFP. Certain Government Furnished Information identified in Section J is authorized under Distribution Statement C and will not be publicly posted to SAM.gov. Authorized Offerors requiring access to these documents shall submit a written request by email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist. Following verification of the requester�s authorization to receive the material, the Government will transmit the applicable documents through DoD SAFE.

title: TECHNICAL SERVICES for NRL 8100 DIV
description: The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL), Code 8124, Advanced Operations Section, intends to procure engineering and technical support services for the design, development, implementation, modification, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of specialized research and development equipment. The contractor shall provide qualified personnel, technical expertise, supervision, management, equipment, tools, materials, and other necessary resources to support operations at the NRL Code 8124 Pomonkey Facility in La Plata, Maryland, and an associated Outside Continental United States (OCONUS) facility. The required services include, but are not limited to: - Support and maintenance of full-motion and limited-motion parabolic antenna systems. - Radio frequency (RF), microwave, waveguide, coaxial, fiber-optic, and network transmission systems. - Electrical, mechanical, electromechanical, and control systems. - Precision fabrication, machining, installation, and modification of specialized equipment and components. - Radome, HVAC, dehumidification, and environmental-control systems. - Backup generators, uninterruptible power systems, telecommunications, CCTV, and related infrastructure. - Preventive and corrective maintenance, testing, calibration, and operational-readiness support. - Technical documentation and configuration management. The Government anticipates awarding a purchase order consisting of firm-fixed-price labor Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), with separately identified cost-no-fee CLINs for materials and travel. The anticipated period of performance consists of a twelve (12) month base period and four (4) twelve-month option periods. **NAICS Code:** 541330 - Engineering Services **Place of Performance:** Naval Research Laboratory, Code 8124, Pomonkey Facility, 7425 Bumpy Oak Road, La Plata, MD 20646, and an associated OCONUS facility. description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought Notice/RFI � Ready Building, Fort Bliss, Texas DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP) or an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This notice is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Construction and Repair) and is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). No solicitation is available at this time. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding Design-Build to Budget (DBtB), project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support the upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The planned procurement will construct a Ready Building, Project Number 570628, at Biggs Army Airfield, Fort Bliss, El Paso, Texas. The project will provide a permanent, properly sized Ready Building supporting continuous, 24-hour operations for an on-call Air MEDEVAC crew. The facility will provide approximately 4,836 square feet of permanent single-story construction. The facility will provide operational space for a five-person aircraft crew, living and readiness space for one five-person crew, and surge capacity for an additional five-person crew. The facility must enable aircraft crews to remain postured for rapid response, with direct access to the aircraft parking apron for MEDEVAC launches and weekend aircraft maintenance. The existing temporary facility is undersized and is not adjacent to the aircraft parking apron. The existing facility will remain operational until construction of the new Ready Building is complete. The temporary facility is outside the new construction footprint and is included in the project demolition scope after completion of the new facility. The project site is adjacent to the Biggs Army Airfield aircraft parking apron. The project site is anticipated to fall within a seismic design condition that may result in Seismic Design Category D requirements. The final Seismic Design Category will be determined by the project Designer of Record in accordance with applicable codes and project-specific site conditions. The Ready Building is a Risk Category IV facility because of its emergency-response function. The project must comply with applicable Unified Facilities Criteria, antiterrorism/force-protection, fire/life-safety, seismic, cybersecurity, and installation requirements. Fort Bliss utility systems are privatized. Required services include electric power, natural gas or an approved alternative fuel approach, water, sanitary sewer, and telecommunications. Utility-system owners are anticipated to provide and own required connections to the facility service disconnect or other defined point of demarcation. The civil utility plan identifies a need for utility-owner rerouting of water and gas around the proposed lid pond. title: Request for Information: Air Operations Center (AOC) Common Air Defense Picture (CADP)
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify existing and emerging software-enabled capabilities that can improve air and missile defense planning, situational awareness, reporting, readiness analysis, sustainment analysis, and decision support. Current workflows require personnel to consolidate information from multiple systems, data sources, and manual processes. This fragmentation can increase manual workload, delay access to relevant information, and complicate collaborative planning and decision support across command-and-control organizations. The Government seeks information on commercial capabilities that can improve access to authorized information, reduce manual reconciliation and reporting burden, and provide authorized users with a more integrated operational picture. The desired capability should support users operating at multiple echelons of command and control while preserving Government decision authority and existing authoritative command-and-control functions.

title: R702--National Longitudinal Survey and Data Management of Psychiatric and Social Health
description: SUBJECT: Notice of Intent to Sole Source National Longitudinal Survey and Data management of Psychiatric and Social Health DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to award, on a sole source basis, a non commercial, cost reimbursement (cost only, no fee) requirements contract to the University of Michigan, Survey Research Center (SRC), 1109 Geddes Ave Ste 3300, Ann Arbor, MI 48109 1015. The requirement is to design, program, and administer a national, longitudinal mental health survey using the Composite International Diagnostic Interview, fifth version (CIDI 5.0) for the VA Central Office, Homeless Programs Office (HPO), National Center on Homelessness Among Veterans (NCHAV). Services include survey instrument programming, mixed mode data collection (web/CATI), probability based sampling with Veteran oversampling, data security, quality assurance, and delivery of cleaned datasets and survey weights for baseline and follow up waves. RATIONALE SUMMARY: The University of Michigan is the only known responsible source with validated access to CIDI 5.0 and proven capability to program and administer this proprietary diagnostic instrument. Market research indicates that no other vendors possess the required CIDI 5.0 expertise or the ability to conduct a full probability national longitudinal survey with Veteran oversampling. Attempting to transition this work to another vendor would result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays. title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

title: Request for Information for U-2 Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System -2
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, manufacturing, engineering, software development, maintenance and experience to meet qualification requirements to repair and sustain the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS)-2 components and ground support equipment. The level of security clearance and amount of overseas continental united states participation in this requirement has not been determined. The Government does not own or have access to the data for ASARS-2 sensor. The Government has determined that this system is a noncommercial item. Contractor shall furnish all material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, and services. The contractor is responsible for providing, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at their facility or a subcontractor�s facility. Contractor furnished material or parts used for replacement shall equal or exceed the quality of the original material or parts. Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. The Air Force requires long-term support and sustainment of the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS) -2, which provides near-real-time high-resolution, long-range imagery from ground returns during day or night, in all weather conditions. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. This effort requires cybersecurity support and sustainment in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 503, and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) process, Cybersecurity Impact Evaluation Recommendation (CIER) for all changes and modifications of this effort to incorporate in the U-2S Approval to Operate (ATO) package, Cybersecurity Authorization Package (CAP), Risk Management Framework (RMF), Interim Authority to Test (IATT), Interim Authority to Connect (ATC), and/or separate ATO, as applicable and requested by the Government. This effort also requires Depot Maintenance Support Teams (DMST) to support the following sustainment activities: mission software updates; Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) engineering; engineering change proposals; configuration management (hardware and software); integration with ASARS-related systems on the U-2 platform; data management; technical data (such as technical manuals and reports) development and maintenance; in-plant Specialized Repair Activity and sparing; technical and engineering actions for calibrating ASARS-2; resolving system failures/issues in a timely manner; and planning/preparation/implementation of system sustainment improvements.

title: Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day
description: Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day Important Dates: Industry Day Registration Deadline -- 3:00 PM EDT on Friday, November 13, 2026 Industry Day -- 9:00 AM EDT on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 1. Introduction For over 10 years, TSA has held regular events to engage with external aviation security stakeholders, including airports, airport designers, airlines, equipment vendors, industry groups, and other domestic and international industry stakeholders in support of TSA�s mission. TSA has capitalized on these events to: Promote TSA�s checkpoint system of systems designs and standards; Encourage collaboration within the aviation security community; Share best practices from a variety of operating environments, facility sizes, and capabilities; Learn about the latest security technology advances and industry innovations; and Engage with stakeholders early in the design process to allow TSA to influence designs and support public-private partnerships. 2. Purpose The Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day is a forum for engaging the communities implementing aviation security in a collaborative environment, consistent with TSA strategic priorities to Improve Security, Safeguard the Transportation System, and Accelerate Action. 3. Event Description: Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026 9:00 AM EDT Location: Virtual (Microsoft Teams) TSA intends to cover updates related to the Checkpoint Requirements and Planning Guide (CRPG), the Planning Guidelines and Design Standards (PGDS), and Donations. 4. Agenda (See attached) 5. Required Criteria for Attendance: Participation in the Industry Day is limited to representatives from the following organization categories: a. Transportation security equipment manufacturers; b. Checkpoint designers; c. Checked baggage inspection system designers; d. Systems integrators; e. Airlines; f. Airport authorities; g. Aviation industry associations; and h. Federal, state, and local government entities. To be considered for attendance, each responding organization must submit a one- to three-sentence summary describing its relevant experience and any other pertinent information demonstrating that it qualifies under one or more of the categories listed above. 6. Registration: The following information must be submitted (with the information in Section 5) to CheckpointRequirements@tsa.dhs.gov no later than 3:00 PM EDT on Friday, November 13, 2026 in the format below: Attendee First Name, Attendee Last Name, Agency/Company/Airport, Attendee Email Address/ Category/Categories per Section 5, one- to three-sentence summary describing Relevant Experience and any other pertinent information demonstrating qualification under the referenced category. TSA will send a confirmation email with Industry Day details to those who are accepted by TSA to attend this Industry Day. Acceptance from TSA for attendance at this event is subject to TSA�s sole review and discretion. Satisfaction of the Required Criteria for Attendance, registration for the event, and acceptance by TSA is required. 7. Post Industry Day Any questions or comments after the industry day should be directed to CheckpointRequirements@tsa.dhs.gov. **Disclaimer- This Industry Day is being held for market research and industry engagement. Attendance is voluntary and the Government will not pay for attendance or travel. Organizations responding to this announcement are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their responses to this announcement and with attendance.**

title: TECHNICAL SERVICES for NRL 8100 DIV
description: The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL), Code 8124, Advanced Operations Section, intends to procure engineering and technical support services for the design, development, implementation, modification, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of specialized research and development equipment. The contractor shall provide qualified personnel, technical expertise, supervision, management, equipment, tools, materials, and other necessary resources to support operations at the NRL Code 8124 Pomonkey Facility in La Plata, Maryland, and an associated Outside Continental United States (OCONUS) facility. The required services include, but are not limited to: - Support and maintenance of full-motion and limited-motion parabolic antenna systems. - Radio frequency (RF), microwave, waveguide, coaxial, fiber-optic, and network transmission systems. - Electrical, mechanical, electromechanical, and control systems. - Precision fabrication, machining, installation, and modification of specialized equipment and components. - Radome, HVAC, dehumidification, and environmental-control systems. - Backup generators, uninterruptible power systems, telecommunications, CCTV, and related infrastructure. - Preventive and corrective maintenance, testing, calibration, and operational-readiness support. - Technical documentation and configuration management. The Government anticipates awarding a purchase order consisting of firm-fixed-price labor Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), with separately identified cost-no-fee CLINs for materials and travel. The anticipated period of performance consists of a twelve (12) month base period and four (4) twelve-month option periods. **NAICS Code:** 541330 - Engineering Services **Place of Performance:** Naval Research Laboratory, Code 8124, Pomonkey Facility, 7425 Bumpy Oak Road, La Plata, MD 20646, and an associated OCONUS facility. Interested vendors shall review the complete solicitation, including all attachments, for detailed performance requirements, personnel qualifications, quotation instructions, and evaluation criteria. **Solicitation Number:** N00173-27-Q-0002 **Quotation Due Date:** November 13, 2026 **Contracting Point of Contact:** Torrean J. Green Contract Specialist Naval Research Laboratory, Code 1330 Email: torrean.j.green.civ@us.navy.mil All questions concerning this solicitation shall be directed to the Contracting Point of Contact identified above.

title: Solicitation_S-280C/G Vehicle Mounted Shelter
description: ***29 OCT 2026 - AMD 0004 issued*** ***20 OCT 2026 - AMD 0003 issued*** ***13 OCT 2026 - AMD 0002 issued*** ***10 SEP 2026 - AMD 0001 issued*** The Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) to establish a new five-year, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the manufacture and delivery of four (4) variants of the S-280C/G Vehicle Mounted Shelter. This is a non-commercial requirement. Requirement: The S-280C/G is a lightweight, tactical military shelter designed to house and protect sensitive electronic equipment and personnel. Manufacturing shall be in strict accordance with the Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) and ASTM E1975-22. The scope includes First Article Testing (FAT), production, and delivery of all associated technical and logistics data. National Stock Numbers (NSNs): 5411-01-304-3069 (Shielded) and 5411-01-092-0892 (Unshielded). Set-Aside: This is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The applicable size standard for NAICS 332311 is 750 employees. Award Basis: The Government intends to award a single IDIQ contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This will be a tradeoff source selection conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15. Contract Value: The minimum guaranteed value for this contract is $100,000.00. The maximum estimated contract ceiling is $4,000,000.00. Technical Data Package (TDP): The TDP for this solicitation is Export-Controlled (Distribution Statement C). To gain access, interested parties must have a current and valid DD Form 2345, "Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement" certification on file with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office (JCO). The TDP can be accessed through the attachments section of this announcement on SAM.gov by certified offerors. Questions: All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing to the points of contact listed below no later than September 24, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Points of Contact: Nicholas A. Lang, Contract Specialist, nicholas.a.lang.civ@army.mil Daniel J. Gibson, Contracting Officer, daniel.j.gibson43.civ@army.mil Disclaimer: Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any amendments to this solicitation.

title: F-35 GAU-22 and F/A-18 M61 Range Data Acquisition System
description: This announcement should not be construed as a commitment by the U.S. Government. The U.S. Navy does not intend to award a contract based on this Request for Information/Sources Sought Notice. THIS IS NOT A Request for a Proposal AND DOES NOT OBLIGATE THE U.S. GOVERNMENT TO ISSUE an RFP. This RFI is for U.S. Government planning purposes only and constitutes requests for exchange of information pursuant to FAR Part 10. The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), Contracts Department, Code 02 is conducting Market Research on an F-35 GAU-22 and F/A-18 M61 Range Data Acquisition System. NSWC IHD is conducting a market survey to identify sources/vendors capable of supplying a system satisfying the following requirements: The system shall consist of an integrated test and control console, computer workstation, and junction box capable of controlling and monitoring performance data for F/A-18 A/A49A-1, A/A49A-2 and F-35 GPU-8/A, GPU-9/A gun pods. The system shall interface with and control the 20mm M61A1/A2 gun in the F/A-18 A/A49A-1 and A/A49A-2 gun system configurations and must include an integrated lane-capable Gun Control Unit (GCU). The system shall interface directly with the standard GPU-8/A and GPU-9/A Gun Systems Control Unit (GSCU) for controlling 25mm gun pods. Manual swapping of control and telemetry cables between gun platforms is acceptable provided all connectors and bulkheads are military or industrial grade and rated for high-cycle insertion and removal. The system shall replicate the baseline gun acceptance output, logging, and monitoring instrumentation utilized at production gun test facilities. The data points monitored shall include: Gun rate Trigger signal Arm signal Safing signal Steady state rate Acceleration and deceleration time Hydraulic flow rate Hydraulic pressure for supply and return Hydraulic fluid temperature Hydraulic fluid temperature Hydraulic fluid pressure Rounds fired Rounds cleared The RDAS setup shall operate strictly using existing test range utility power supplies: 115 VAC, 1-Phase, 60 Hz 300 VDC, 2.0 A 28 VDC, 30.0 A The hardware must incorporate a hardwired, fail-safe "dead-man switch" accessible to the Range Safety Officer (RSO). Releasing the switch at any point during active operations shall immediately disarm the weapon drive and inhibit fire control commands. The Contractor shall provide a complete Operational and Maintenance Manual covering the custom console, software configuration, cabling schematics, calibration procedures, safety interlocks, and troubleshooting. System Drawings & Calibration Records: Applicable factory calibration data, wiring schematics, and system interconnection drawings shall accompany final hardware delivery. The Contractor shall provide hands-on operational training, integration, and dry-fire range demonstration at the Picatinny Arsenal test range following installation. The Contractor shall live fire test the system with an F/A-18 A/A49A-1 or A/A49A-2 gun system and an F-35 GPU-8/A or GPU-9/A gun pod to verify proper function prior to delivery to the government. Government test facilities are not available for live fire testing as this capability has not been established yet. Request your company provide responses to the following questionnaire: Does your company have the capability to meet all of the requirements mentioned above? If yes, describe your company's history and experience with supplying this item (or similar gun control systems). Can your company provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) price estimate? What is your company�s plan for live fire verification testing with applicable gun systems? Does your planned testing facility hold the necessary ATF licensing, Net Explosive Weight (NEW) storage capacity, and compliance with DoD 4145.26-M to perform the live fire verification testing? All interested sources shall provide the organization name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, business size, Unique Entity ID, and CAGE Code. In addition, all interested sources shall provide a summary of their company�s capabilities and delivery timeframe and schedule. All responding sources must email their response submissions no later than 16:00 Eastern Time on 13 November 2026 to the Point of Contacts (POCs) listed below. title: National Architect-Engineer Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice only. This notice does not constitute a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), Request for Proposals (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB), nor does it represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. This Sources Sought Synopsis is issued solely for market research and planning purposes to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources. It is not a Request for Proposals or Quotes and imposes no obligation on the Government to acquire any goods or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government reserves the right to determine the appropriate acquisition approach based on the results of this market research. Responders should not anticipate feedback regarding their submissions. The Government will not pay for any costs incurred in responding to this Synopsis; all costs associated with responding are solely at the responding party's expense. The information provided herein is subject to change and is non-binding on the Government. The purpose of this notice is to conduct market research to identify potential and qualified sources, assess industry capabilities, and establish effective acquisition strategies, including potential small business set-aside opportunities. No reimbursement will be provided for any costs associated with submitting information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. Overview The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is conducting market research to establish Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for comprehensive, multidisciplinary Architect-Engineer (A/E) services. These contracts are intended to provide integrated, sustainable, and adaptive design solutions across federally owned and leased real property nationwide. The Government anticipates awarding multiple contracts with multi-year ordering periods (5 year base with one 5 year option) to support GSA zones and client agencies across the United States and its territories. Expected typical project size is to be above the simplified acquisition threshold of $350,000. The potential place of performance for services rendered under this contract is on an as-needed basis for federal projects anywhere in the United States and its territories. This will require the capability to travel to GSA and other Government agency office locations nationwide. In some instances, performance of services is expected to require the capability for contractors to dispatch personnel to multiple locations simultaneously. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541310 (Architectural Services) & 541330 (Engineering Services), which has a small business size standard of $12.5 million and $25.5 million respectively. Specialized Technical & System Design - Work requested often involves the assessment, repair, and upgrade of existing complex building systems. Required AE Disciplines and Expertise - AE firms will need staff with licensed and/or specialized expertise in the following disciplines: Core Architectural and Engineering Disciplines Architecture and Interior Architecture Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Structural & Civil Engineering, and Plumbing Historic Preservation Specialized Expertise A Qualified/Licensed Fire Protection Engineer (NCEES)* Security Space Planning & Workplace Cost Estimating and Scheduling Environmental Services Modernization and Quality Control Building Information Modeling (BIM) Quality control review and Report writing Submission Requirements Interested firms are invited to submit a written Capability Statement. Business size status under NAICS 541310 or 541330 (Large Business or Small Business). B. Relevant Experience Summarize three to five (3�5) relevant projects completed within the past ten (10) years. Demonstrate experience in projects of similar scale, scope, and complexity, such as federal workplace design, major repairs and alterations, or complex building systems. Include project title, customer/agency point of contact, contract value, role (Prime or Subcontractor), and a brief narrative of the work performed. C. Nationwide Capacity Demonstrate organizational capacity to manage and execute multiple task orders simultaneously across diverse geographic locations nationwide. Describe key disciplines maintained in-house versus those typically fulfilled through subcontractor or joint venture arrangements. Submission Instructions Responses must be submitted electronically via email to the primary procurement contacts listed below: Submission Deadline: Primary Contact: Point of Contact Email: Subject Line Format: Sources Sought Response - National A/E IDIQ - [Firm Name] Hard copies, telephonic inquiries, and late submissions will not be reviewed or acknowledged. All information provided in response to this notice will be used strictly for market research and acquisition planning purposes. title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: In accordance with the Commercial Solutions Opening � Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA), posted October 2, 2026, under Notice ID HQCAAA2701, the following requirement supports Area of Interest (AoI) 5.1 Accelerate Eligible Patron Growth. The parent CSO with instructions is located at Related ID HQCAAA2701. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for a digital storefront, in-store fulfillment, and delivery solution(s), hereinafter referred to as �DeCA2U�. The primary goal of DeCA2U is to deliver a seamless, modern, and fully integrated omnichannel grocery experience for authorized patrons at Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) locations in the contiguous United States (CONUS), Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico that matches or exceeds the best commercial grocery services available today. The DeCA2U solution shall utilize a market-aligned commercial financial model typical of leading grocery retailers. The prospective contractor shall identify all locations in which it could provide an entire end-to-end solution enabling authorized patrons to place grocery orders, make payment, and receive their groceries at a designated delivery location. Specifically, DeCA2U will provide one unified, easy-to-use platform enabling authorized patrons and military units to: Shop and order groceries online anytime, anywhere via mobile app or website; Receive accurate real-time inventory and pricing from their local commissary; Benefit from fast, accurate in-store picking and professional order assembly; Enjoy reliable, tracked doorstep delivery directly to their home or quarters or convenient curbside pickup; Track and be rewarded for purchases; Leverage value-added functionality like forgotten items, �People who bought this� recommendations, menu building, price checking, or any other shopping experience enhancement capability; and Complete transactions through a secure, seamless payment process supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT). The Government reserves the right to add payment options. Offerors shall propose pricing reflecting current commercial market rates for similar omnichannel. The Service Contract Labor Standards (formerly the Service Contract Act), 41 U.S.C. ��6701 et seq. will be applicable to any resulting contract. The desired outcome is to establish a long-term commercial partnership that provides authorized commissary patrons with a convenient, reliable, and cost-effective grocery shopping experience through an integrated solution for online ordering, payment processing, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery. The solution should leverage proven commercial capabilities, support operational efficiency, enhance the commissary benefit, and provide a scalable and sustainable service model that can adapt to evolving mission requirements and patron needs. Proposed solutions should comply with applicable commercial and/or Department of War (DoW) cybersecurity standards, including but not limited to, SOC 2 Type 2. Additionally, integrated payment and entitlement gateways supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and SNAP EBT. Proposed solutions must meet current commercial PCI DSS compliance and USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) digital security specifications. The platform shall ensure robust end-to-end encryption for data at rest and in transit (FIPS 140-3 validated) and secure patron Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in accordance with federal privacy standards. Solutions shall propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflects customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, and delivery benchmarks for the proposed capability. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government�s discretion. DeCA will not endorse any contractor employee for the purpose of installation access; as such, solutions shall address their proposed approach to meeting applicable military installation access requirements, including personnel screening, credentialing, and delivery access procedures. DeCA will utilize the phased evaluation process established in the overarching Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), Notice ID HQCAAA2701. Interested vendors with demonstrated commercial experience in grocery eCommerce, order fulfillment, pickup, delivery, or integrated retail solutions with foundational information security management system standard should submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in accordance with the applicable submission requirements of the overarching CSO. Solution Briefs should describe: the proposed commercial approach; relevant capabilities; anticipated benefits to DeCA and its authorized patrons; proposed business model; PoP; Service Contract Labor Standards; installation access; and cybersecurity measures. Additionally, all proposed solutions shall address the vendor's ability to integrate with DeCA�s retail ecosystems and scale to DeCA�s business needs. The Government will evaluate submissions in accordance with the criteria established in the overarching CSO and may invite selected vendors to participate in subsequent phases. The closing date for this �Call for Solution� is Friday 13 November 2026 at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). All communications, including solution brief information and submission requirements shall be sent via email to the following Points of Contact: Diana Gross-Bendall, email: diana.gross-bendall@deca.mil and Tinitia Gholson, email: tinitia.gholson@deca.mil.

title: Sensitive But Unclassified-Encrypted (SBU-E) Radio Cybersecurity Industry Day
description: The Department of the Army, representing the Capability Program Executive Command and Control Information Network (CPE C2IN), the Project Manager Command and Control Transport (PM C2T), and the Product Manager Tactical Communication Systems (PdM TCS), has issued a Call for Solutions (CFS) under Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Part 212.70 to establish a 10-year enterprise acquisition framework for innovative tactical communication capabilities. The Army will host an Industry Day event from 1-3 December 2026 to facilitate collaboration and information sharing regarding upcoming security requirements for Sensitive But Unclassified-Encrypted (SBU-E) tactical radios. The primary objective is to brief industry partners on new cybersecurity requirements for SBU-E tactical radios and to provide a collaborative forum for feedback. Participation is limited to federal government employees, support contractors, and industry partners with current federal contracts (FEDCON). Industry partners must limit attendance to three attendees per company. See attachment for more details.

title: BPA CALL for Cultural Resources Investigation Irrigation Pipeline Project
description: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Farm Production and Conservation (FPAC) is issuing this pre-solicitation notice as a means of complying with the USDA's Simplified Procedure policy in FAR Part 5.1. USDA-FPAC intends on awarding a BPA Call Order against: (Cultural Resources Investigation for the proposed Irrigation Pipeline Project in Westfield, Hampden County, Massachusetts. USDA NRCS Massachusetts State Office) for the (Title BPA Holder: 12FPC426A0003). NRCS has planned and designed an irrigation system that would consist of approximately 2,600 feet of 2� diameter PE irrigation pipeline installed at a depth of 4 feet from the ground surface. Because this project is located on or near archeologically sensitive landforms and archeological sites, an intensive ground survey including soil test pits along the length of the proposed pipeline is required. This is not a solicitation. This synopsis notification of intent to award a BPA Call order does not constitute a request for proposals or submission of any information in response to this notification. This procurement is restricted to the approved vendor eligible for call orders under the aforementioned BPA Holder. Competition: This requirement will be requested by one existing Small Business BPA holder under their previously awarded Firm?Fixed?Price BPA: 12FPC426A0003 (Gray and Pape Inc.). These services are for Cultural Resources Investigation in Massachusetts. A Firm?Fixed?Price call order will be issued under the applicable BPA. This BPA call order will remain under the original small business set-aside associated with the BPA Master award. No responses from non?BPA holders will be accepted. The government will not provide feedback or evaluations to companies regarding their submissions in response to this notice. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes under FAR Part 5; it does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred in preparation of responses to this notice. title: Secret But Unclassified-Encrypted (SBU-E) Radio Cybersecurity Industry Day
description: The Department of the Army, representing the Capability Program Executive Command and Control Information Network (CPE C2IN), the Project Manager Command and Control Transport (PM C2T), and the Product Manager Tactical Communication Systems (PdM TCS), has issued a Call for Solutions (CFS) under Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Part 212.70 to establish a 10-year enterprise acquisition framework for innovative tactical communication capabilities. The Army will host an Industry Day event from 1-3 December 2026 to facilitate collaboration and information sharing regarding upcoming security requirements for Sensitive But Unclassified-Encrypted (SBU-E) tactical radios. The primary objective is to brief industry partners on new cybersecurity requirements for SBU-E tactical radios and to provide a collaborative forum for feedback. Participation is limited to federal government employees, support contractors, and industry partners with current federal contracts (FEDCON). Industry partners must limit attendance to three attendees per company. See attachment for more details.

Special Notice and Disclaimer THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. THE SUBMISSION OF PRICING, CAPABILITIES FOR PLANNING PURPOSES, AND OTHER MARKET INFORMATION IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). DISCLAIMER This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, invitation for bid, or promise to issue a future solicitation. IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information, participating in discussions, or otherwise responding to this notice. Submission of a response is voluntary and is not required to compete for any future acquisition. Failure to respond will not prevent an entity from participating in a future solicitation. The Government may use submitted information to refine its requirements, acquisition strategy, socioeconomic approach, pricing structure, ordering procedures, and performance standards. Respondents should clearly mark proprietary, confidential, or competition-sensitive material; however, respondents should avoid submitting classified information or unnecessary personally identifiable information. PLEASE READ THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION IN ITS ENTIREITY. 2. Purpose Department of Veterans Affairs, National Cemetery Administration is conducting market research to determine the availability, capability, capacity, geographic reach, and interest of businesses able to provide recurring and nonrecurring grounds maintenance services at NCA National Cemeteries throughout the United States and its territories. The Government is considering a nationwide, multiple-award indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract under which specific requirements would be ordered through task orders. The Government seeks industry input for the following: Feasibility of a nationwide acquisition: Determine whether a single nationwide contract or acquisition approach is practical, including whether vendors have geographic reach, staffing, infrastructure, and operational capacity to support requirements across the country. Competition and small-business participation: Assess the number and types of potential offerors, as well as opportunities for small businesses to compete as prime contractors, subcontractors, or teaming partners. For example, respondents may identify whether requirements should be set aside or divided to encourage meaningful small-business participation. Regional structures: Identify effective ways to divide the requirement, such as national, state, district, or regional. See Addendum A. Respondents can describe which division is more effective in enhancing services, reducing travel or logistics costs, increasing competition, improving performance outcomes and increasing quality standards. Respondents should recommend measurable performance objectives, service-level requirements, quality standards, and methods for evaluating results. Pricing method and economic price adjustment: This will be a firm fixed price contract. Respondents should also address factors that may justify economic price adjustments, such as changes in labor rates, material costs, fuel prices, inflation, or applicable wage requirements. Mobilization, surge, subcontracting, and reporting capabilities: Describe the ability to begin performance within the required timeframe, increase capacity during periods of unusually high demand, manage subcontractors, and provide accurate and timely reports. Examples include transition staffing plans, emergency-response capacity, subcontractor oversight, performance dashboards, and standardized monthly reports. Barriers to competition, cost, or successful performance: Identify conditions that could limit competition, increase prices, delay implementation, or create performance risks. Examples may include overly restrictive experience requirements, insufficient lead time, geographic coverage challenges, workforce shortages, unclear requirements, data limitations, security or facility-access constraints, and burdensome contract terms. 3. Background and Anticipated Acquisition The contemplated vehicle would support a diverse portfolio of Government-owned or Government-operated National Cemeteries/Soldier s Lots. Site characteristics, acreage, climate, terrain, security conditions, service frequency, and local requirements may vary substantially. Contract Type Multiple-award IDIQ, subject to market research and acquisition approval Ordering Task orders using firm-fixed price, unit-priced, or other authorized arrangements appropriate to each requirement Potential Period Base and Five, One Year Option Periods Geographic Coverage Nationwide United States, District of Columbia, and potentially U.S. territories and possessions Potential Award Structure National, State, District, or Regional Estimated Ceiling To Be Determined Guaranteed Minimum To be established in any resulting solicitation and contract 4. Anticipated Scope of Services Task orders may require some or all of the following services. The final scope, frequencies, standards, quantities, and site-specific conditions would be identified in the applicable task-order performance statement. The anticipated Scope of Services may include, but is not limited to, the following activities: Memorial and monument services: Installation, and setting of upright headstones, flat markers, niche markers, private markers, and monuments. Headstone services: Raising, lowering, realignment, resetting, and fine-tuned alignment of headstones and other memorial markers. Memorial cleaning and maintenance: Cleaning, preservation, and routine maintenance of headstones, markers, monuments, and related memorial features. Grounds maintenance: Gravesite and turf maintenance, including mowing, trimming, edging, and other routine grounds-care activities. Pest control: Inspection, treatment, monitoring, and prevention of pests affecting the grounds, plantings, structures, and related facilities. Landscape maintenance: Maintenance of trees, shrubs, planting beds, ornamental plantings, and associated landscape features. Irrigation, pond, and drainage services: Inspection, operation, maintenance, repair, and related services for irrigation systems, ponds, drainage systems, and associated components. Waste and debris removal: Removal and disposal of trash, leaves, branches, clippings, and other debris from gravesites, grounds, paved areas, and facilities. Pavement care: Sweeping, cleaning, and routine maintenance of roads, walkways, parking areas, and other paved surfaces. Artificial turf maintenance: Cleaning, grooming, infill maintenance, weed control, and related upkeep of artificial turf areas. Winter services: Ice prevention and the removal of snow and ice from roads, walkways, parking areas, entrances, and other designated surfaces. Structure and facility services: Cleaning of structures, janitorial services, and light maintenance necessary to keep facilities clean, safe, and operational. Ceremony assistance: Setup, coordination, site preparation, and related assistance for ceremonies and scheduled events. Winter

title: Request For Proposal (RFP) NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen 4 (NANO 4)
description: UPDATE - 11/03/2026 The purpose of this update is to post amendment 8 to the RFP. SUBMISSION DUE DATE FOR THE 2027 OPT-IN IS CHANGED, FROM: FRIDAY, 11/06/2026, 4:30PM EST. TO: FRIDAY, 11/13/2026, 4:30PM EST. **************************************************************** UPDATE - 10/28/2026 POSTING QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS FOR: 2027 NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen (NANO) 4 Opt-in Opportunity UPDATE - 10/07/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen (NANO) 4 opt-in opportunity as described in the original NANO 4 Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 RFP was issued on March 4, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2, Clause 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and Clause 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 contract�s ordering period remains valid through June 30, 2029. The RFP resulted in the award of six indefinite delivery (ID) fixed price with Economic Price Adjustment (FPEPA) requirements contracts with fixed price delivery orders for the supply of liquid nitrogen and liquid oxygen in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. NASA made award to the following companies: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc., Airgas USA LLC (Central), Airgas USA LLC (South), Linde, Inc., Nippon Sanso Matheson, Inc. (formerly Matheson Tri-gas, Inc.), and Messer LLC. Each year during the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from new entrants for each IDIQ subCLIN location and the Government will also accept proposals from existing NANO 4 contractors for each additional proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. A new entrant does not hold a current NASA liquid nitrogen or liquid oxygen contract. The Government will evaluate the proposals to determine technical acceptability for a specific NASA location. Upon the Government�s determination of technical acceptability, a contract (for new entrants) or contract modification (for existing NANO 4 Contractors) will be executed to add the Contractor to the IDIQ CLIN Pool for the specific NASA location. Thereafter, the Contractor will be eligible to participate in the IDIQ CLIN Pool process described in Section 2.8 for the NASA locations awarded to that Contractor. All eligible Contractors who are awarded an IDIQ subCLIN for a particular NASA location will have the option to compete for requirements within those IDIQ subCLINs which they are awarded. The commodities will support current and future aerospace flight, simulation, research, development, testing, and other operations at the following NASA centers and facilities: Ames Research Center (ARC), Moffett Field, CA 94035; Glenn Research Center (GRC), Cleveland, OH 44135; GRC/Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (ATF), Sandusky, OH 44870; Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Greenbelt, MD 20771; Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Pasadena, CA 91109; Johnson Space Center (JSC), Houston, TX 77058; Kennedy Space Center (KSC), Kennedy Space Center, FL, 32899; Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS), Cape Canaveral, FL, 32920; Langley Research Center (LaRC), Hampton, VA 23666; Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, AL, 35812; Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF), New Orleans, LA 70129; Stennis Space Center (SSC), Stennis Space Center, MS, 39529; White Sands Test Facility (WSTF), Las Cruces, NM 88012 and other such places of performance as required in this contract. Submission information: 1. Opt-in by a Current NANO-4 Contractor. A current NANO-4 Contractor shall submit 2027 Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in RFP Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Liquid Nitrogen and Liquid Oxygen � Requirements. If the Contractor is determined technically acceptable, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). 2. Opt-in by New Entrant. The new entrant shall submit an Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in RFP Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Liquid Nitrogen and Liquid Oxygen � Requirements. Once determined acceptable from a technical standpoint, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). New entrants will be required to comply with the provisions of Section 2.5 of the RFP and all terms and conditions of the resulting contract. 3. All questions regarding this opt-in notice shall be submitted in writing via email to Rose Dougherty at rose.a.dougherty@nasa.gov. The Government will not answer oral questions due to the possibility of misunderstanding or misinterpretation. The Offeror shall submit all questions, if any, no later than October 21, 2026, to allow for analysis and dissemination of responses in advance of the proposal due date. The Government will not guarantee a response to late questions. Questions shall not be directed to technical personnel. 4. It is requested that any interested party notify the NANO 4 Contracting Officer via email no later than October 21, 2026, of your intent to submit a proposal during this opt-in period as well as the name(s) of which NASA Center(s) you intend to propose. Please send your notice of intent to propose to Rose Dougherty at rose.a.dougherty@nasa.gov. 5. All offers shall be sent to Rose Dougherty at rose.a.dougherty@nasa.gov by 4:30PM EST, November 6, 2026. Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, paragraph (f). 6. An ombudsman has been appointed in accordance with NFS 1852.215-84. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Update - 4/22/20024 This update is to post amendment 7 to the RFP. Amendment 7, reopens the RFP and notifies offerors that the Government�s requirements for CLIN 24 and subCLIN 26.24 for Stennis Space Center, have changed. This amendment updates the RFP and resolicits with the updated requirements for CLIN 24 and subCLIN 26.24 only. Offerors are invited to propose on CLIN 24 for Stennis Space Center (SSC) liquid oxygen support. When submitting your proposal use the revised Attachment 6 Price Proposal Template Amendment 7 and follow the solicitation provision 6.3(b) Submission of offers. Offerors are also invited to submit Attachment 2.1 Capability Form-IDIQ subCLINs for subCLIN 26.24 SSC liquid oxygen support. Proposals submitted prior for CLIN 24 and subCLIN 26.24 are no longer valid and new proposals must be submitted. All offerors interested in this CLIN and/or subCLIN should submit a proposal by Thursday April 25, 2024 at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time. No other proposal revisions will be accepted. ____________________________________________________________ Update - 4/5/2024 This purpose of this update is to post amendment 6 to the RFP, and to post questions and responses regarding the RFP. Responses must be accompanied by descriptive literature, warranties and/or other information that demonstrates that the offer meets all the foregoing requirements. JUSTIFICATION FOR THE PROPOSED SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION: GE Healthcare is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and the sole source capable of providing the comprehensive preventive maintenance and repair services required for the Government-owned Discovery MI DR PET/CT Scanner. While the physical hardware may be present, the operational software architecture, predictive diagnostics, and advanced sub-system calibration protocols are strictly proprietary intellectual property owned exclusively by GE Healthcare. Utilizing an unauthorized third-party maintenance provider to service the scanner will immediately render existing service frameworks and software licensing agreements void, introducing severe operational, safety, and regulatory risks to the instrument's performance. All servicing personnel must be factory-trained and certified directly by GE Healthcare, possessing specific, continuous experience on this exact model that unauthorized third-party biomedical technicians completely lack. Introducing a new, uncertified contractor at this juncture would critically disrupt the Molecular Imaging Branch's (MIB) ability to perform daily diagnostic scanning on cancer patients enrolled in time-sensitive clinical trials, as an outside vendor cannot guarantee emergency response times, provide requisite software patches, or deliver necessary clinical applications support. The Discovery MI DR PET/CT system relies on a direct, secure, and encrypted remote network connection to GE Healthcare known as InSite. This proprietary platform allows GE Healthcare engineers to remotely monitor the PET/CT scanner in real time, view diagnostic error logs, isolate system anomalies, and deploy remote service repairs. This direct digital pipeline drastically decreases scanner downtime and cannot be accessed, licensed, or replicated by any third-party firm. Furthermore, the required service agreement covers technical and clinical applications telephone support provided directly by GE Healthcare specialists, which is an invaluable and non-replicable asset when constructing new patient research protocols. The agreement also provides exclusive end-user access to TiP-Ed Online, a proprietary clinical continuing education platform, and GE iCenter, a cloud-based asset maintenance and management software application. The iCenter platform tracks complete service and maintenance histories specifically for this Discovery MI DR PET/CT scanner, supporting critical workflow management, regulatory compliance, and improved patient outcomes. Because these essential cloud applications, remote diagnostic keys, and intellectual property rights are contractually non-transferable, they cannot be sub-licensed, bypassed, or passed through an unauthorized third-party broker. Consequently, GE Healthcare is the only source legally and technically capable of fulfilling this requirement.
