title: Italy – Refuse disposal and treatment – Procedura aperta, ai sensi dell'art. 71, d.lgs. 36/2023, articolata in n. 4 lotti, per l'affidamento del Servizio di raccolta, trasporto, smaltimento e/o recupero dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti e luoghi di produzione della RAI S.p.A. di Roma, Torino, Milano e Napoli
description: L’appalto ha ad oggetto il servizio di raccolta, trasporto, smaltimento e/o trattamento/recupero dei rifiuti speciali (pericolosi e non pericolosi), prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai, comprensivi dei relativi cantieri e set esterni, localizzati nelle città di Roma, Torino, Milano e Napoli e relative zone limitrofe il cui elenco è dettagliato nel progetto di servizi. Saltuariamente l’attività di raccolta, trasporto, smaltimento e/o trattamento/recupero dei rifiuti, potrà avvenire su tutto il territorio italiano per quanto concerne i cantieri e set esterni (come, ad esempio, per la manifestazione del Festival di Sanremo). Il servizio si articola nelle seguenti fasi: a) supporto; b) analisi di caratterizzazione del rifiuto; c) movimentazione interna; d) raccolta; e) pulizia delle aree; f) trasporto; g) conferimento; h) intermediazione; i) smaltimento; j) recupero. Rientra nell’appalto, altresì, la fornitura di contenitori vuoti e di contenitori aggiuntivi nonché l’etichettatura e la cartellonistica. Al fine di garantire il contemperamento tra la necessità di i) favorire la massima partecipazione e l’accesso delle MPMI, nonché, comunque, ii) razionalizzare la spesa ed efficientare il processo d’acquisto, ai sensi di quanto previsto dall’articolo 58, comma 4, d.lgs. 36/2023, ciascun concorrente – pur potendo presentare offerta per tutti i lotti in cui è articolata la gara - non potrà aggiudicarsi più di un lotto; la relativa aggiudicazione avverrà seguendo l’ordine decrescente dell’importo economico dei lotti, partendo dal valore più alto. Qualora non fosse possibile procedere all’aggiudicazione di uno o più lotti per mancanza di offerte ad esito di quanto sopra previsto, la stazione appaltante, al fine di assicurare il soddisfacimento del fabbisogno, si riserva la facoltà di aggiudicare gli eventuali lotti residui anche in deroga al suddetto limite di aggiudicazione, laddove risultassero offerte valide presentate da concorrenti già aggiudicatari di un lotto, purché in possesso dei relativi requisiti. In particolare, il servizio ha ad oggetto la trattazione delle seguenti tipologie di Codici EER: - Codici passivi, per i quali il fornitore riceverà un importo per la quantità (Kg, Litri o Metri cubi, ovvero numero di ritiri nel caso dei rifiuti ambulatoriali e sanitari) di rifiuto effettivamente trasportato e conferito a destinazione finale. L’importo unitario per ciascun codice è da intendersi comprensivo anche delle spese di carico, trasporto e conferimento; - Codici a titolo gratuito, per i quali il servizio sarà svolto dall’aggiudicatario senza il pagamento di un corrispettivo; - Codici attivi, per i quali l’appaltatore corrisponderà alla RAI il corrispettivo indicato in sede di offerta e valido per l’intera durata del Contratto. Per la dettagliata descrizione delle caratteristiche tecniche e funzionali del Servizio nonché delle modalità di esecuzione dello stesso e del dettaglio delle sedi di intervento si rimanda al Progetto di Servizi. Ai sensi dell’art. 58 del Codice, l’appalto è suddiviso nei seguenti n. 4 lotti: o Lotto n. 1: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Roma; o Lotto n. 2: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Torino; o Lotto n. 3: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Milano; o Lotto n. 4: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Napoli. Tenuto conto dei principi in materia, il perimetro di ciascun lotto è stato definito applicando un criterio geografico per un bilanciamento tra obiettivi diversi: mantenere una logica di continuità territoriale per la preminente esigenza connessa ad un efficiente gestione della prestazione contrattuale e, al contempo, consentire la partecipazione alle microimprese, piccole e medie imprese (MPMI) in grado di modulare la propria offerta in relazione a potenziali specificità territoriali. Non si è ritenuto di procedere ad un’ulteriore frammentazione delle prestazioni all’interno dei singoli ambiti territoriali, in quanto le attività oggetto di affidamento presentano una forte integrazione operativa, gestionale ed amministrativa e richiedono un coordinamento unitario nell’ambito del medesimo insediamento. Un’ulteriore suddivisione avrebbe potuto determinare inefficienze gestionali, sovrapposizioni organizzative e maggiori oneri di coordinamento contrattuale, senza apportare significativi benefici in termini di apertura del mercato.

description: Обект на настоящата обществена поръчка е „услуга” по смисъла на чл.3, ал.1, т.3 от Закона за обществените поръчки („ЗОП“) с наименование: „ИЗБОР НА ОПЕРАТОР ЗА ЕКСПЛОАТАЦИЯ И ПОДДРЪЖКА НА ИНСТАЛАЦИИТЕ ЗА СЕПАРИРАНЕ И КОМПОСТИРАНЕ НА РЕГИОНАЛНО ДЕПО ЗА ТВЪРДИ БИТОВИ ОТПАДЪЦИ „ТЕКЛЕН ДОЛ“ НА ГРАД СМОЛЯН“. Поръчката предвижда избор на оператор за експлоатация и поддръжка на Регионално депо за твърди битови отпадъци „Теклен дол“ на град Смолян. Изборът на оператор по реда на ЗОП се обуславя от конкретните изисквания на нормативната уредба, в това число Закона за управление на отпадъците („ЗУО“) и Наредба № 6 от 27.08.2013 г. за условията и изискванията за изграждане и експлоатация на депа и на други съоръжения и инсталации за оползотворяване и обезвреждане на отпадъци, свързани със следните основни дейности с данни за индикативните им количества за 36 /словом: тридесет и шест/ месеца, както следва: 1) Приемане на отпадъци по кодове съгласно Комплексно разрешително („КР“) № 358-Н0/2008г., актуализирано с решения № № 358-Н0-И0-А1/2016 г. и 358-Н0-И0-А2/2022 г., на Община Смолян за Регионално депо за неопасни отпадъци на общините Смолян, Чепеларе и Баните; Третиране на отпадъци по кодове съгласно Комплексно разрешително („КР“) № 358-НО/2008 г., актуализирано с решения № № 358-Н0-И0-А1/2016 г. и 358-Н0-И0-А2/2022 г.; Транспортиране на отпадъците от инсталацията за сепариране до клетка № 3, а след извеждането ѝ от експлоатация – до клетка № 2; и Транспортиране на подситова фракция до площадка. Индикативно количество: 51 000 тона. 2) Приемане и шредиране на зелени и биоразградими отпадъци в инсталацията за компостиране и производство на компост при спазване на съответната технология за производство на компост, на техническия проект за изграждане на обект: „Реконструкция и модернизация на регионално депо за твърди битови отпадъци Смолян“ и на условията по Комплексно разрешително („КР“) № 358-НО/2008 г., актуализирано с решения № № 358-Н0-И0-А1/2016 г. и 358-Н0-И0-А2/2022 г.. Индикативно количество: 15 000 тона. 3) Транспортиране и предаване на гориво от отпадъци до посочена от изпълнителя и одобрена от възложителя инсталация за изгаряне с оползотворяване на енергията, респ. площадка за обезвреждане на отпадъка. Индикативно количество: 15 000 тона. Забележка: Индикативното разстояние за транспортиране и предаване на гориво от отпадъци, което възложителят е приел с оглед определяне на стойността на договора за изпълнение на обществената поръчка, е 160 км /словом: сто и шестдесет километра/ (посоченото разстояние е определено с оглед местоположението на най-близката регистрирана инсталация за изгаряне на гориво от отпадъци с оползотворяване на енергията). Това разстояние не е обвързващо за изпълнителя, като одобряването от възложителя на инсталация за изгаряне с оползотворяване на енергията, респ. площадка за обезвреждане на отпадъка се извършва на база на критерии най-близко транспортно разстояние от регионалното депо за твърди битови отпадъци за общините Смолян, Чепеларе и Баните и действителни възможности за приемане на гориво от отпадъци. Определените от възложителя количества на отпадъците по отделните видове дейности са индикативни, като същите служат единствено за определяне на индикативната стойност на договора за изпълнение на обществената поръчка и по никакъв начин не ангажират възложителя да ги усвои, както и по никакъв начин не ограничават дейностите по изпълнението в техните рамки при генериране на отпадъци над определените от възложителя индикативни количества, като подлежат на заплащане единствено действително изпълнените съгласно условията на договора за изпълнение на обществената поръчка видове и количества дейности.

title: TSA PreCheck Travel Industry Partnership Request for Information
description: 1. DESCRIPTION Background: The TSA TTC Office is requesting information and conducting market research to understand the level of interest from industry, particularly travel industry partners such as airlines and other travel-related companies, in partnering with TSA to increase TSA PreCheck enrollments. Objectives: TSA�s primary objective is to expand TSA PreCheck participation by increasing the total number of program members, also known as Known Traveler Number (KTN) holders. The TSA PreCheck program provides significant benefits to both TSA and its members, including enhanced security, improved checkpoint efficiency, and a better passenger experience. TSA currently has approximately 50 million Known Traveler Number holders and believes this number could double with industry support. TSA is requesting information on potential concepts, capabilities, and partnership models to grow the TSA PreCheck program through collaboration with airlines, other travel industry companies, and/or other interested parties. The travel industry has unique access to individuals as they are considering travel, making reservations, preparing for a trip, or engaging in other travel-related activities. These interactions may position travel industry entities to effectively promote TSA PreCheck and encourage eligible travelers to begin and complete enrollment. TSA is interested in receiving open-ended responses from industry regarding how partners could help increase TSA PreCheck enrollments. TSA does not intend to prescribe a single approach. Instead, TSA seeks information on a range of potential concepts that may include, but are not limited to, marketing, customer engagement, referral models, incentives, bundled offerings, online enrollment support, integration with existing travel platforms, enrollment event support, or other innovative concepts proposed by respondents. Industry partners may propose approaches that identify individuals who do not have a Known Traveler Number, engage customers during travel-related interactions, and encourage or support the TSA PreCheck enrollment process. Depending on the proposed approach, industry partners may collect limited information from interested individuals, such as name, date of birth, and preferred contact information, including email address and/or phone number. Industry partners may also propose other data collection, referral, voucher, payment, or enrollment support concepts for TSA�s consideration. Individuals enrolling in TSA PreCheck would still be required to complete an in-person enrollment through one of TSA�s three authorized enrollment providers, CLEAR, IDEMIA, or Telos. TSA is interested in learning more about capabilities that would allow industry partners, including airlines and travel industry companies, to market, promote, facilitate, refer, incentivize, or otherwise support TSA PreCheck enrollments. TSA is also interested in understanding how industry partners would measure results, report activity, support reconciliation, and structure compensation for efforts that result in increased TSA PreCheck enrollments. Industry partners may receive payment for activities that successfully support TSA PreCheck enrollment growth, subject to any future agreement and applicable requirements. TSA is seeking industry input on potential pricing structures, including, but not limited to, per-enrollment payments for completed enrollments, fixed-fee arrangements, milestone-based pricing, or other pricing concepts proposed by respondents. RESPONSES TO THIS RFI This section identifies the key information TSA requests from respondents. The topics below are intended to minimize respondent effort and help structure responses for ease of Government review. Respondents should also address the following topics, as applicable. Respondents are encouraged to propose their own concepts and are not limited to the examples provided. Response Element Description of Requested Information Illustrative Examples 1. Marketing Concepts Describe the concepts or capabilities the respondent believes could grow the TSA PreCheck population. Responses should explain how the proposed approach would reach, inform, encourage, or support travelers who may be interested in enrolling in TSA PreCheck Examples may include general TSA PreCheck marketing, targeted marketing, customer engagement during booking or trip preparation, referral programs, TSA PreCheck-specific benefits or bundles, loyalty program concepts, enrollment incentives, digital engagement strategies, temporary enrollment event support, or other innovative concepts. 2. Proposed Solution Description Describe the proposed solution or solutions to identify, engage, refer, capture, or otherwise support travelers interested in enrolling in TSA PreCheck. Respondents should explain the proposed customer journey and how the approach would support enrollment from initial engagement through completion, as applicable. For example, a respondent could propose a referral model in which a traveler is directed to an authorized enrollment provider and the partner receives payment if the traveler completes enrollment. A respondent could also propose capturing payment at the time of booking and providing the potential applicant with a voucher code that could be redeemed for enrollment. 3. Data Collection, Referral, and Transmission Approach Describe any proposed data collection, customer engagement, referral, payment, voucher, and transmission processes based on The respondent�s recommended technical and business approach. TSA has not yet finalized the minimum biographic data elements that industry partners may be required to collect and submit under any future approach. Depending on the proposed solution, TSA anticipates that this information may include name, date of birth, and preferred contact information. Respondents may also propose approaches that involve additional biographic information, payment information, referral information, voucher codes, or other data elements, as appropriate. Examples may include collecting limited biographic data, collecting additional biographic data such as passport number, address, or citizenship/permanent resident status, capturing payment information, issuing voucher codes, transmitting referral information, integrating with TSA�s authorized enrollment providers, or using another method to support the enrollment process. 4. Collaboration with Other Entities Identify whether the respondent intends to collaborate with other entities in support of the proposed concept. If so, describe the anticipated role of each entity. Examples may include collaboration with TSA�s current authorized enrollment providers, airlines, airports, travel agencies, online booking platforms, loyalty program providers, credit card issuers, or other travel industry companies. 5. Enrollment Completion Strategies and Incentives Describe any strategies the respondent may use to encourage travelers to complete the TSA PreCheck enrollment process after expressing interest or beginning an application. If applicable, describe any additional benefits the respondent may offer to encourage TSA PreCheck enrollment. Examples may include follow-up reminders, targeted communications, discounts, loyalty benefits, bundled travel benefits, targeted promotions, temporary enrollment event support, or other incentives. 6. Enrollment Impact Provide estimates of the number of individuals who may enroll in TSA PreCheck as a result of the proposed partnership. Respondents should include any assumptions used to develop those estimates. Examples of supporting assumptions may include estimated audience size, number of travelers without a Known Traveler Number, expected engagement rate, referral rate, application initiation rate, enrollment completion rate, campaign duration, or expected enrollment volume by channel. 7. Pricing Model and Assumptions Provide proposed pricing information for the respondent�s industry partnership

title: Submarine Rescue Operations Maintenance Contractor (SROMC)
description: The Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Undersea, managed through the Direct Reporting Program Manager (DRPM) Submarines intends to issue a solicitation for continued support of operation and maintenance of the U.S. Navy Submarine Rescue System (SRS) which will transition to an International Association of Classification Societies (IACS) commercial classification system as directed by Director, Undersea Warfare Division (OPNAV N97). The SRS is a highly portable and mobile submarine rescue and recompression system capable of transferring personnel from a Distressed Submarine (DISSUB) under pressure from depths up to 2,000 feet seawater. The U.S. Navy SRS is composed of the Pressurized Rescue Module System (PRMS), the Submarine Decompression System (SDS), the Assessment/Underwater Work System (AUWS) and other critical ancillary support equipment. The Submarine Rescue Operations Maintenance Contractor (SROMC) is responsible for: maintaining all systems in a constant high state of readiness; providing appropriate and sufficient personnel and services necessary for the engineering, management, technical and logistic support, mobilization, deployment, operation, storage, and repair; and maintenance of the SRS on a 24-hour-per-day, 7-day-a-week basis. The Government will rely and follow applicable federal procurement rules and regulations including the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and the Navy Marine Corps Acquisition Regulation Supplement (NMCARS) for the planned acquisition. PAE Undersea/DRPM intends to solicit this requirement as a full and open competition. A solicitation is expected to be released on or around November 2026. The contemplated contract will include one base year with four option years, for a total of 60 months if all options are exercised. The contract type is anticipated to be a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Level of Effort and Cost only. All responsible sources may submit a proposal, which shall be considered by the Navy. The Navy plans to issue a solicitation electronically via Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) and prospective offerors must comply and follow the instructions in the solicitation. Interested offerors are hereby encouraged to monitor PIEE and www.SAM.gov for the anticipated release of the solicitation, and any associated amendments. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for award. This synopsis is hereby issued in accordance with RFO 5.101(c) and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government is not accepting proposals as a result of this synopsis. The Government will not reimburse for any costs or expenses associated with questions submitted or information provided in response to this notice. The Government intends to host a site visit to discuss operations, maintenance, and modernization of the U.S. Navy?s SRS. A special notice with additional information and details will be issued electronically via PIEE and www.SAM.gov.

All work shall be completed in accordance with applicable codes, manufacturer instructions, and agency standards to provide a fully operational and complete HVAC system. title: H141--Animal Lab Air Changes per Hour (ACH) & Pressure Testing
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6 on behalf of Richmond VA Medical Center is conducting Market Research through this Sources Sought notice to help determine the availability of qualified Businesses, capable of providing service for Animal Lab Air Change per Hour (ACH) and Pressure Testing that meets the following requirements: The contractor shall verify ACH levels in all designated lower-level research/animal laboratory rooms. The contractor will confirm pressure relationships between rooms and adjacent corridors/spaces. The contractor shall identify deficiencies and perform corrective adjustments, as needed. The contractor will provide complete documentation of airflow measurement, ACH calculations, and pressure results. The contractor will complete all specific tasks as stated below. The contractor shall provide all tools, equipment, consumable materials, labor, transportation and supervision. Specific Taks: The contractor measure supply, return, and exhaust airflow quantities required to compute ACH for each room. The contractor shall verify and document pressure differentials (positive or negative) per room relative to adjacent corridors/spaces. The contractor shall conduct testing in accordance with NEB Procedural Standards, VA regulations, and any federal, state, and local standards and regulations. The contractor shall conduct the following adjustments and balancing: Evaluate any rooms failing to meet ACH or pressure criteria. Perform corrective adjustments using existing HVAC controls and balancing devices. Retest rooms following adjustments and provide updated results. The contractor shall deliver a comprehensive report, including: Individual room airflow measurements. ACH calculations and compliance assessment. Pressure relationship findings. List of rooms not meeting specified performance requirements. Recommendations for any repairs or modifications beyond the scope of TAB adjustments. Any repairs or modifications completed. Deliverables: Final ACH and Pressure Verification Report (PDF format). Summary of deficiencies and recommended corrective actions. Updated airflow/pressure logs post-adjustments. Signed certification by NEBB-certified TAB professional. All respondents shall indicate/provide the following: Whether or not they are small business manufacturers of the products they wish to offer, or if they are a reseller of a small business manufacturer. Is your company interested in providing a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) quote or Open Market (indicate FSS contract #)? Identify any other companies owned (wholly or in-part) by the owners of this business who provide goods or services under the same or a related NAICS codes. Identify any other companies owned (wholly or in-part) by the owners of this business who provide goods or services that are registered under the same or a related NAICS code with the Center for Veterans Enterprise (CVE); Provide the certification type (SDVOSB/VOSB), Federal Identification Number, and state of incorporation for each. Whether or not your company has an active SAM registration and the companies Unique Entity Identifier. A copy of its capabilities statement. Failure to provide the above information may result in the potential offeror being considered incapable of meeting the VA s needs. If the contractor can provide the above items, the contractor shall provide a letter from the manufacturer stating they are an authorized distributor/licenser of their products. Failure to submit an authorized distributor letter shall result in the product(s) potentially offered to be considered grey market and shall not be considered technically acceptable. The capability statements received from this market research are for planning purposes only and will assist the Government in planning its acquisition strategy. This is strictly market research, and the Government will not entertain questions concerning this market research. The Government will not assume any costs incurred by the contractor in the preparation of responses. All responses shall be submitted in writing no later than November 13, 2026, at 5:00 PM EST to the attention of: Natasha.Hawkins@va.gov Please title the subject line for responses as: Animal Lab ACH and Pressure Testing.

Government answer to RFC 01 is also posted. ________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF), Bremerton, Washington intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of one (1) Edgecumbe RCD Barge. The Edgecumbe RCD Barge characteristics are 240 FT length, 60 FT width, 2 FT 11 IN Draft, 928 L Tons full displacement, 48 years of age, and hull material is steel. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of accommodating one (1) Edgecumbe RCD Barge with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officers Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish zinc anode replacement; preliminary and final air tests of all tanks/voids; tank/void open, clean and gas free; and support ABS and USCG inspections. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 15 December 2026 - 19 February 2027. This is full and open competition. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Request for White Papers: Intelligence Resource Execution and Oversight (Project Argus)
description: Intelligence Resource Execution and Oversight (Project Argus)- HQ0034279R001 Area of Interest: The Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (USW(I&S)) requires a prototype solution to replace the legacy Budget and Intelligence Related Database (BIRD). USW(I&S) is responsible for overseeing intelligence resource execution across the Department. The current BIRD system, developed and maintained by multiple contractor teams over more than a decade using disparate technology stacks and evolving priorities, now suffers from outdated software frameworks, inefficient code, and an overly complex database schema. These deficiencies impede timely analysis, increase manual workload, and limit the ability of analysts to support senior leader decision-making on intelligence resources. USW(I&S) seeks a modern, flexible, and extensible system that enables efficient ingestion, cataloguing, analysis, and visualization of intelligence resource data. The desired end-state is a single, user-friendly platform that supports rapid querying, analytic dashboards, and an intuitive interface (including special intelligence-enabled natural language queries) so that analysts can produce accurate, timely insights and the Congressional Justification Book (CJB) with significantly reduced manual effort. The prototype solution must deliver the following core capabilities (additional modules may be required based on evolving USW(I&S) priorities): Ingestion and management of current and historical Intelligence Resource data and execution data. Data will be uploaded by multiple users spanning the Department of War, i.e. Agencies and Services. Access to and ability to upload shall be controlled by the Office of the USW(I&S). Financial management query tool and data analytics supported by Super Intelligence so users can interact with the database for in-depth analysis. This tool should have the ability to create data visualizations. User defined Visual Dashboard creation capability that utilizes resource data uploaded into the system database. Congressional Justification Book (CJB) Generator capable of combining quantitative data and narrative inputs from both internal and external stakeholders to produce the CJB. This tool shall take input from users spanning the Department of War, i.e. Agencies and Services. Access to and ability to input shall be controlled by the Office of the USW(I&S). System should operate at multiple classification levels, i.e. development at an UNCLASSIFIED level that is transferable to the SECRET and TOP SECRET networks; data held at a lower level should be replicated to the higher level. Specific Modules: CJB Execution Countries of Interest tracking Congressional Marks tracking Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDC) data management The system must be able to ingest data from common formats (including Microsoft PowerPoint, PDF, and Excel). Offerors may propose either cloud-based or on-premise solutions (or a hybrid approach). Any proposal must include a clear comparison of the pros and cons of the proposed hosting approach, including considerations of cost, security, performance, scalability, and transportability. The solution must support development in an unclassified environment while remaining transportable and operable across Impact Levels (IL) 2 through 7. USW(I&S) requires direct, on-site engagement between the development team and government analysts throughout the prototype effort to ensure the solution meets operational needs. In the event that the proposed system is not ready for deployment by September 2027, respondents must address their ability to sustain the legacy BIRD system on-site within its classified environment while finalizing the new system. Additionally, respondents must outline their approach to providing the required minimum of 12 months of on-site sustainment following successful transition to ensure full system operability and rapid response. Special Considerations: Place of Performance: For development, the primary places of performance will be the Pentagon and a contractor-provided development site. If required to sustain BIRD, the primary place of performance will be the Pentagon. Travel and Remote Work: Alternate work locations are authorized for development activities. Direct, on-site engagement between the development team and government analysts is required throughout the prototype effort to ensure the solution meets operational needs. Situational telework may be approved on a case-by-case basis. CONUS travel is authorized as mission needs require and is subject to Government approval. Security: Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) facility clearance and personnel clearances are required. Personnel supporting classified development, sustainment, or analytic functions shall possess the appropriate clearance level for their role, up to and including Top Secret / SCI. Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, and Regulatory Compliance: The solution must comply with all applicable Department of War and Intelligence Community cybersecurity, information assurance, and related requirements. This includes, but is not limited to, the Risk Management Framework (RMF); National Institute of Standards and Technology; Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM); Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs); software version update strategies to remain compliant with DISA Standard Parts List (SPL); and relevant DoD Instructions (including DoDI 8500.01 and DoDI 8510.01). The performer shall support the Government in obtaining and maintaining the necessary Authorizations to Operate (ATO) across Impact Levels (IL) 2 through 7. Please see the attachment for more information and the white paper template. Please submit your company's white paper to Ms. Ashley Brink (ashley.a.brink.civ@mail.mil) and Ms. Carrie Martin (carrie.e.martin13.civ@mail.mil) NLT 05:00pm EST on November 13, 2026.

description: This is notice of an upcomming contracting opportunity and site visit. A site visit has been scheduled for 11/19/2026 at 0930. Interested parties MUST follow instructions below in order to gain access to DSCR; it is a secure facility and access is permitted ONLY to those who have been vetted and approved. NOTE: This contracting opportunity is for door repair service at Defense Supply Center Richmond. The resultant contract will be an Indefinite Delivery Purchase Order(IDPO). This notice is being published at this time in order to allow adequate time for vetting of persons interested in attending the upcomming site visit. In order to attend the site visit interested parties MUST follow the instructions below no less than 5 business days prior to the site visit. This is to allow time for vetting by base security. Plan on arriving at DSCR an hour prior to the site visit time, as the processing time through the visitor center fluctuates. Follow the link below to register through DBIDS, and a QR code should be provided for each visitor. The QR codes MUST be emailed to the Project Manager, Mike O'Connor <Michael.OConnor@dla.mil> (Work Cell: 804-306-5273). The QR code MUST be emailed to the project manager as soon as possible due to the lengthy vetting process of approximately 5 business days. The project manager will also serve as the sponsor for site visit attendees. A new system was implemented on 3 January 2023 to screen visitors and contractors for installation access at DSCR.The new system is designed to increase efficiencies, enhance the protection of personal information during the vetting process and eliminate the use of hard copy DLA Form 1815s. The new screening system will require visitors and contractors to pre-enroll in DBIDS (Defense Biometric Identification System). To begin the process, visitors and contractors will complete registration through the pre-enrollment website: https://dbids-global-enroll.dmdc.mil. Upon entry of their information, visiting personnel will be provided an electronic form to download, which will have an individualized barcode and alpha numeric code. The codes need to be sent to the visiting person�s sponsor(Mike O'Connor). Once in receipt of the barcode, the sponsor will email Security and Emergency Services and provide the barcode and sponsorship information. Once the visitor/contractor is vetted and approved for installation access, Security & Emergency Services will notify the sponsor that the visitor/contractor can go to the DSCR Visitor Center to obtain his/her pass. At the Visitor Center, the visitor provides the barcode and code provided earlier in the process and completes the credentialing process. See attached SOW for full requirement details. Parties interested in this project are advised and expected to have reviewed the entire SOW prior to site visit attendance. This notice of an upcomming contracting opportunity which will be awarded as an indefinite delivery purchase order(IDPO) for door repair service at Defense Supply Center Richmond. The full solicitation will be published on, or around, 11/09/2026 and will remain open for a period not less than 30 days. A site visit will be held on 11/19/2026 at 0930. See map on p.49 of the attached Statement of Work(SOW) for the meeting location for the site visit.

title: Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS) Production
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT SEEKING OR ACCEPTING UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS. This notice is a Request for Information (RFI) as defined in FAR 15.101(c). The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) is conducting market research for the Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS). ACNS helps to determine vessel position based on optical sighting of celestial objects including stars and resident space objects (RSOs) such as satellites and space debris. Ship�s position derived from ACNS shall be used to improve the resilience of the surface ship Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) system of systems suite by providing an Alternative Position Source (APS) to support Assured PNT. U.S. Navy and commercial enterprises leverage a variety of navigation solutions that allow vessels to safely navigate with and without GPS. The U.S. Navy is looking to modernize legacy systems over time. This RFI seeks information on prospective technologies that could be leveraged or developed as enablers for an ACNS solution. This RFI seeks to understand how interested parties would integrate the ACNS with navigation sensors and other ship equipment specifically Global Positioning System-Based Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Service (GPNTS). PAE MS invites all interested potential sources, including small business concerns, to submit written information sufficient to demonstrate the respondent�s ability to fulfill the requirements. For those interested parties that have technologies which may not achieve a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 8-9 by FY 2029, please provide information on current research and development efforts that may address some or all requirements of this RFI beyond FY 2029. Responses are requested by 13 November 2026. Questions or clarifications related to this RFI may be submitted electronically to Ms. Liz Bonilla-Sotomayor at liz.c.bonilla-sotomayor.civ@us.navy.mil and Ms. Andrea Longo at andrea.t.longo.civ@us.navy.mil. Verbal questions will not be accepted. Questions shall not contain classified information. Please ensure that the subject line of any emails containing responses or questions related to this notice includes the name of your firm and �Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS) RFI Response� (without quotation marks) in the subject line. title: CPE CBRND Seeking Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) on Aluminum Flakes for Screening Obscuration Module - Multispectral (SOM-M)
description: 1.0 Disclaimer This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the U.S. Government (USG) to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the USG will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this RFI. Responders are advised that the USG will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. The information gathered by this RFI will be shared with relevant interested USG parties to help inform future development and procurement efforts. 2.0 Background The Joint Product Manager for CBRN Layered Effects is responsible for enabling and enhancing the survivability of our Joint Warfighters so they can fight and win across all domains in a CBRN-contested environment. As the acquisition leader in mobile analytics, our portfolio provides transformative solutions � including advanced reconnaissance systems, sensors, and mobile analytical laboratories � that ensure our military is safeguarded against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats. To support this mission, the USG is pursuing the Screening Obscuration Module - Multispectral (SOM-M) program, which is envisioned as a modular, man-portable, ground-emplaced obscuration and screening system designed to produce a multispectral obscurant cloud for both mounted and dismounted use. In support of the SOM-M program, the USG is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify alternative, cost-effective commercial manufacturing options for critical, novel bispectral obscurant material. The technical requirements for this capability are detailed in Section 4.0 of this document. 3.0 Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to survey industry capabilities and identify alternative commercial manufacturing options for a novel bispectral obscurant material. Specifically, the USG seeks to identify manufacturers capable of performing high-volume Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) onto Aluminum Flakes at a commercial scale, and to assess industry readiness to support a potential Army-funded manufacturing maturation project aimed at reducing sustainment costs. 4.0 Technical Requirements Interested parties must demonstrate capabilities or conceptual pathways to meet the following production and material requirements: Base Material & Size: Aluminum Flake sized at 2 � 4 microns. Coating Process & Material: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) onto the aluminum flakes. Target Production Volume: Scalable to large commercial quantities, ranging from hundreds of pounds (lbs) to tons. Cost Efficiency: Proposed alternative manufacturing options must significantly reduce current manufacturing protocol costs to ensure long-term sustainment capability for the military services. 5.0 Requested Information Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI providing a white paper including technical insights on the manufacturing feasibility, cost-effectiveness, and scalability of the proposed Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) process. Ideal responses will include the following elements: Manufacturing/Production Approach: A comprehensive overview of the proposed methodology to achieve the PVD coating of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) on Aluminum Flakes (2 � 4 microns). This should include details on the facility scale, equipment, and proposed lead times based on the scale of material produced. Cost Projections & Scale: Estimated cost profiles and projected cost-reduction curves when scaling production from hundreds of pounds to tons, demonstrating how the approach achieves a sustainable cost profile for long term acquisition. Maturity, Capacity, & Risks: An assessment of current facility readiness, current and potential production capacity, and identified technical and manufacturing challenges or risk factors associated with scaling this specific PVD coating process. Company Information & Past Performance: A brief summary of relevant company experience, facility capabilities, or prior similar material coating efforts. 6.0 Submission Requirements All submissions must be electronic and adhere to the following formatting and content rules: Page Limit: All responses shall be no longer than five (5) pages. Formatting: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages, with font size no smaller than 10-point. Company Information: Include official company name, address, telephone number, website, and business type (large/small business classification), CAGE Code. Point of Contact: Provide the name, title, telephone number, and email address of the authorized company representative. 7.0 Submission Guidance Submission Deadline: Responses are requested no later than 5 PM EST Friday, 13 November 2026. Submissions and/or questions should be emailed directly to the following point of contact: Emily McGill, Contract Specialist, emily.c.mcgill.civ@army.mil Samantha Degele, Contracting Officer, samantha.l.degele.civ@army.mil

title: Overhead Door Repair IDPO; Defense Supply Center Richmond(DSCR)
description: This is notice of an upcomming contracting opportunity and site visit. A site visit has been scheduled for 11/19/2026 at 0930. Interested parties MUST follow instructions below in order to gain access to DSCR; it is a secure facility and access is permitted ONLY to those who have been vetted and approved. NOTE: This contracting opportunity is for overhead door repair service at Defense Supply Center Richmond. The resultant contract will be an Indefinite Delivery Purchase Order(IDPO). This notice is being published at this time in order to allow adequate time for vetting of persons interested in attending the upcomming site visit. In order to attend the site visit interested parties MUST follow the instructions below no less than 5 business days prior to the site visit. This is to allow time for vetting by base security. Plan on arriving at DSCR an hour prior to the site visit time, as the processing time through the visitor center fluctuates. Follow the link below to register through DBIDS, and a QR code should be provided for each visitor. The QR codes MUST be emailed to the Project Manager, Mike O'Connor <Michael.OConnor@dla.mil> (Work Cell: 804-306-5273). The QR code MUST be emailed to the project manager as soon as possible due to the lengthy vetting process of approximately 5 business days. The project manager will also serve as the sponsor for site visit attendees. A new system was implemented on 3 January 2023 to screen visitors and contractors for installation access at DSCR.The new system is designed to increase efficiencies, enhance the protection of personal information during the vetting process and eliminate the use of hard copy DLA Form 1815s. The new screening system will require visitors and contractors to pre-enroll in DBIDS (Defense Biometric Identification System). To begin the process, visitors and contractors will complete registration through the pre-enrollment website: https://dbids-global-enroll.dmdc.mil. Upon entry of their information, visiting personnel will be provided an electronic form to download, which will have an individualized barcode and alpha numeric code. The codes need to be sent to the visiting person�s sponsor(Mike O'Connor). Once in receipt of the barcode, the sponsor will email Security and Emergency Services and provide the barcode and sponsorship information. Once the visitor/contractor is vetted and approved for installation access, Security & Emergency Services will notify the sponsor that the visitor/contractor can go to the DSCR Visitor Center to obtain his/her pass. At the Visitor Center, the visitor provides the barcode and code provided earlier in the process and completes the credentialing process. See attached SOW for full requirement details. Parties interested in this project are advised and expected to have reviewed the entire SOW prior to site visit attendance. This notice of an upcomming contracting opportunity which will be awarded as an indefinite delivery purchase order(IDPO) for overhead door repair service at Defense Supply Center Richmond. The full solicitation will be published on, or around, 11/09/2026 and will remain open for a period not less than 30 days. A site visit will be held on 11/19/2026 at 0930. See map on p.49 of the attached Statement of Work(SOW) for the meeting location for the site visit.

title: Netherlands – Gully cleaning and emptying services – Reinigen kolken en lijngoten - Oost Gelre
description: Op basis van een dienstverleningsovereenkomst verzorgt ROVA in de gemeente Oost Gelre het reinigen van kolken en lijngoten in de openbare ruimte. In de gemeente Oost Gelre reinigt ROVA jaarlijks alle gemeentelijke kolken. Een deel van de werkzaamheden voert ROVA in eigen beheer uit en een deel van de werkzaamheden wordt op de markt gezet (uitbesteed). NV ROVA Holding organiseert een Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure voor het contracteren van één aannemer voor de uitvoering van het bestek voor het reinigen van kolken en lijngoten in de gemeente Oost Gelre. De opdracht omvat jaarlijks het reinigen van circa 13.600 kolken in de reguliere reinigingsronde en circa 900 kolken in een aanvullende reinigingsronde. Daarnaast worden meerdere malen per jaar lijngoten en bijbehorende zandvangputten gereinigd. De werkzaamheden omvatten tevens de afvoer en verwerking van vrijkomend rioolslib. De genoemde hoeveelheden zijn indicatief en gebaseerd op de bestekshoeveelheden.

title: Netherlands – Sewer cleaning services – ROK Reinigen en Inspecteren riolering DOWR 2027-2030
description: De hoofdriolering van de gemeente Deventer, Olst-Wijhe en Raalte heeft onderhoud nodig. Om de staat van de riolering in beeld te hebben moet er jaarlijks gereinigd en geïnspecteerd worden. Daarvoor brengen de gemeenten dit onderhoudscontract op de markt. De gemeenten hebben per jaar gemiddeld een budget voor het reinigen en inspecteren. Het budget wordt als taakstellend gezien. De omvang van de opdracht kan als gevolg van areaalwijzigingen en budgetwijzigingen wijzigen, met dien verstande dat de omvang van de opdracht het plafondbedrag niet te boven kan gaan. Omvang: Perceel 1, Deventer, jaarbudget ca. € 300.000, plafondbedrag € 1.800.000,- (4 jaar). Perceel 2, Olst-Wijhe, jaarbudget ca. € 50.000, plafondbedrag € 300.000,- (4 jaar). Perceel 3, Raalte, jaarbudget ca. € 120.000, plafondbedrag € 720.000,- (4 jaar).

title: Greece – Training services – Δράσεις Κατάρτισης και Πιστοποίησης Εργαζομένων
description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι η αναβάθμιση δεξιοτήτων των επικουρικών διασωστών – πληρωμάτων ασθενοφόρων του ΕΚΑΒ, μέσω κατάλληλης εκπαίδευσης και πιστοποίησης. Αντικείμενο του έργου είναι η υλοποίηση ενός προγράμματος συνεχιζόμενης αναβάθμισης δεξιοτήτων των επικουρικών διασωστών – πληρωμάτων ασθενοφόρων του ΕΚΑΒ με τα παρακάτω αντικείμενα: Το φυσικό αντικείμενο θα περιλαμβάνει: - την ανάπτυξη εκπαιδευτικού υλικού - την κατάρτιση οκτακοσίων πενήντα (850) ατόμων μέσω εκατόν εβδομήντα (170) ωρών εκπαίδευσης, εκ των οποίων οι ογδόντα (80) ώρες θα πραγματοποιηθούν μέσω της σύγχρονης και ενενήντα (90) ώρες μέσω ασύγχρονης εκπαίδευσης σε διάφορες θεματικές ενότητες - πιστοποίηση των καταρτιζόμενων και - δράσεις δημοσιότητας. Η παρούσα σύμβαση χρηματοδοτείται από Πιστώσεις του Προγράμματος Δημοσίων Επενδύσεων (Συλλογική Απόφαση ΣΑΝΑ391, Ενάριθμος Έργου 2025ΝΑ39100002). Η σύμβαση περιλαμβάνεται στο υποέργο Νο 1 της Πράξης: «Δράσεις ανάπτυξης δεξιοτήτων και ικανοτήτων ανθρωπίνου δυναμικού, Επικουρικών Διασωστών Πληρωμάτων Ασθενοφόρων του ΕΚΑΒ», η οποία έχει ενταχθεί στο Εθνικό Πρόγραμμα Ανάπτυξης 2021-2025 με βάση την Απόφαση Ένταξης με αρ. πρωτ. Α3α/Γ.Π.οικ.10539/05-03-2025 και έχει λάβει κωδικό MIS 5224975. Η παρούσα σύμβαση χρηματοδοτείται από την εθνικούς πόρους μέσω του ΠΔΕ.

title: Bygg- og grunnentreprise Tjeldbergodden transformatorstasjon
description: Tjeldbergodden transformatorstasjon ligger nordøst i Aure kommune på Nordmøre. Nærmeste nabo er Equinor sitt prosessanlegg, rett vest for den nye stasjonstomten. Ny transformatorstasjon skal øst for tomten og industriområdet til Equinor Tjeldbergodden og utformes med: - 132kV AIS-anlegg - En ny transformator - To transformatorsjakter - Stasjonsbygg for 22kV AIS-anlegg - Forberedt for videre utvidelser med føringsveier, fundamenter, osv. ARBEIDENES ART OG OMFANG - Etablering av komplett byggegrop med løsmasseuttak og sprengningsarbeid. - Oppfylling av stasjonstomt med kvalitetsmasser. - Komplett adkomstvei fra eksisterende private veinett hos Equinor og inn til tomt for ny transformatorstasjon. Mindre endringer av [OH1] eksisterende vei for tilpasning for massetransport og transformatortransport. - Komplett VA-anlegg og grøfter på tomt med tilknytning til offentlig nett. Eventuelt privat nett (Equinor) for overvannshåndtering. - Komplett utomhusarbeid innenfor stasjontomtens område. - Stasjonsbygg og plasstøpte transformatorceller i betong. - Plasstøpte betongfundamenter for kontroll- og apparatanlegg. Stålstativer inngår i annen entreprise. - Etablering av komplett utendørs jordingsanlegg med maskenett, ringjord, oppstikk, osv. for jording av alle utendørs apparatanlegg og transformatorer. - Komplett svakstrøm elektroinstallasjoner for stasjonsbygg og utendørs med blant annet belysning, adgangskontroll/monitorering og kameraovervåkning. [OH2] - Komplett sikring med områdesiking, skallsikring, sonesikring, EMP-sikring og elektronisk sikring av det planlagte anlegget iht. prosjekterte løsninger og sikringsnotat. - Komplett VVS-installasjoner for stasjonsbygg. - ITB koordinering i henhold til NS 3935. - Prøvedrift og oppfølging i driftsfase i henhold til NS 6450.
